source.text: ἴδετε ποταπὴν ἀγάπην δέδωκεν ἡμῖν ὁ πατὴρ ἵνα τέκνα θεοῦ κληθῶμεν, καὶ ἐσμέν.

records.literal_gloss: See what sort of love has given to us the Father, that children of God we should be called, and we are.

en.L: See what sort of love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God; and we are.
en.B: Consider the kind of love the Father has given us: we are called children of God, and we really are {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} children.
en.R: Think how much the Father loves us! Because of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} love we are called God's children, and we really are {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} children.

fr.L: Voyez de quel amour le Père nous a fait don : que nous soyons appelés enfants de Dieu ; et nous le sommes.
fr.B: Considérez l’amour que le Père nous a donné : on nous appelle enfants de Dieu, et nous sommes vraiment {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} enfants.
fr.R: Pensez à tout l’amour que le Père a pour nous ! À cause de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} amour, on nous appelle enfants de Dieu, et nous sommes vraiment {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} enfants.

es.L: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} qué clase de amor nos ha dado el Padre: que seamos llamados hijos de Dios; y lo somos.
es.B: {{plural_you:Consideren|Considerad}} qué amor nos ha dado el Padre: se nos llama hijos de Dios, y de verdad somos {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} hijos.
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Piensen|Pensad}} cuánto nos ama el Padre! Por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} amor se nos llama hijos de Dios, y de verdad somos {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} hijos.

sw.L: Angalieni ni upendo wa namna gani ambao Baba ametupatia, hata tuitwe watoto wa Mungu; na sisi ni watoto hao.
sw.B: Fikirini upendo mkuu ambao Baba ametupatia: tunaitwa watoto wa Mungu, na kweli sisi ni watoto {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.R: Fikirini jinsi Baba anavyotupenda sana! Kwa sababu ya upendo {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} tunaitwa watoto wa Mungu, na kweli sisi ni watoto {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.

ko.L: 보십시오, 아버지께서 우리에게 어떠한 사랑을 주셨는지! 우리가 하나님의 자녀라고 불리게 하셨습니다. 그리고 우리는 [정말 하나님의 자녀]입니다.
ko.B: 아버지께서 우리에게 주신 사랑이 어떠한지 생각해 보십시오. 우리는 하나님의 자녀라고 불리고, 우리는 정말로 그분의 자녀입니다.
ko.R: 아버지께서 우리를 얼마나 사랑하시는지 생각해 보십시오! 그분의 사랑 때문에 우리는 하나님의 자녀라고 불립니다. 그리고 우리는 정말로 그분의 자녀입니다.

decisions.choice: what kind of love: love so great that it is a cause for wonder
decisions.reason: ποταπὴν asks about the quality of something, often with a note of amazement (Matthew 8:27; Luke 1:29). The call to "see" invites the readers to stop and wonder at it.

decisions.choice: the clause says what the love consists in: the Father has made us his children, so that we are called by that name
alternatives: purpose: he loved us in order that we might be called his children
decisions.reason: ἵνα here explains the love rather than stating a goal set apart from it: the love is seen in the status it gives. To be "called" in this way is to be given a name that is true (John 1:12), which the next words insist on.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: include "and we are"
decisions.reason: The words are in the early major manuscripts. Many later manuscripts, the majority, leave them out, and the early printed Greek editions followed them, so some older translations lack the phrase. The shorter text may come from a copyist's eye skipping, and the words fit the letter's insistence that being God's children is a present fact (3:2). Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: and we really are his children (Balanced, Readable); Readable also "Because of his love"
alternatives: and that is what we are
decisions.reason: The bare "and we are" can sound like an afterthought in English; "really are his children" carries the emphasis the short clause has after "we should be called". Readable makes the link between the love and the name explicit, following the grammar decision above.

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms; hijos de Dios, no gender span
decisions.reason: Each plural "you" and its verb is the ustedes / vosotros reader setting, as in chapters 1-2. "Hijos de Dios" already includes daughters, as in 1 John 5:2, so it takes no gender setting.

decisions.choice: upendo wa namna gani (L); upendo mkuu (B); jinsi ... anavyotupenda sana (R)
decisions.reason: The word asks what kind of love, and expects wonder at how great it is (m1). Literal keeps the question form "wa namna gani"; Balanced says "upendo mkuu" (great love) and Readable makes it an exclamation, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: watoto wa Mungu
decisions.reason: The Greek word is "children", not "sons", and Swahili "watoto" says that for men and women alike. "Wana" is kept for "Son" (Mwana) in this letter.

decisions.choice: "하나님의 자녀" with no gender span (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: The Greek word here is "children", not "sons", so it is already inclusive and the English has no span; Korean "자녀" is the same, as in the Korean John 1:12.

source.text: διὰ τοῦτο ὁ κόσμος οὐ γινώσκει ἡμᾶς ὅτι οὐκ ἔγνω αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: Because of this the world not knows us, because not it knew him.

en.L: Because of this the world does not know us: because it did not know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: The reason the world does not know us is that it did not know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: The world does not understand who we are, because it did not know God.

fr.L: À cause de ceci le monde ne nous connaît pas : parce qu’il ne {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a pas connu.
fr.B: Si le monde ne nous connaît pas, c’est qu’il ne {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a pas connu.
fr.R: Le monde ne comprend pas qui nous sommes, parce qu’il n’a pas connu Dieu.

es.L: Por esto el mundo no nos conoce: porque no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} conoció a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: La razón por la que el mundo no nos conoce es que no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} conoció a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: El mundo no entiende quiénes somos, porque no conoció a Dios.

sw.L: Kwa sababu hii ulimwengu hautujui: kwa sababu haukumjua {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}.
sw.B: Sababu ya ulimwengu kutotujua ni kwamba haukumjua {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}.
sw.R: Ulimwengu haufahamu sisi ni nani, kwa sababu haukumjua Mungu.

ko.L: 이 때문에 세상이 우리를 알지 못합니다. 세상이 그분을 알지 못했기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 세상이 우리를 알지 못하는 것은 세상이 그분을 알지 못했기 때문입니다.
ko.R: 세상은 우리가 누구인지 알지 못합니다. 세상이 하나님을 알지 못했기 때문입니다.

decisions.choice: "because of this" points forward to the reason given by "because": the world does not know us because it did not know him
alternatives: "because of this" points back: the world does not know us because we are God's children
decisions.reason: John often sets up a reason with διὰ τοῦτο and then states it with ὅτι (John 5:16; 10:17; 12:39). The two readings come to much the same thing: those who are God's children are strangers to a world that does not know their Father.

decisions.choice: the world: humanity organised apart from God and opposed to him
decisions.reason: As in 2:15-17 and John 15:18-19, the world here is the realm that does not know God and hates his people (3:13).

decisions.choice: him: God the Father, named in the previous sentence
decisions.reason: The Father is the nearest person named, and the thought is that the world cannot recognise the children because it never knew their Father. John 16:3 says the same of both: "they have not known the Father, nor me", so the difference is small.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names the person the pronoun refers to, following the meaning decision on the pronoun, so a young reader does not have to look back.

source.text: ἀγαπητοί, νῦν τέκνα θεοῦ ἐσμεν, καὶ οὔπω ἐφανερώθη τί ἐσόμεθα.

records.literal_gloss: Beloved, now children of God we are, and not yet has been revealed what we will be.

en.L: Beloved, now we are children of God, and it has not yet been revealed what we will be.
en.B: Dear friends, we are children of God now, and what we will be has not yet been revealed.
en.R: Dear friends, we are God's children right now. But what we are going to be has not yet been shown.

fr.L: Bien-aimés, maintenant nous sommes enfants de Dieu, et ce que nous serons n’a pas encore été manifesté.
fr.B: Chers amis, nous sommes enfants de Dieu dès maintenant, et ce que nous serons n’a pas encore été manifesté.
fr.R: Chers amis, nous sommes déjà maintenant les enfants de Dieu. Mais ce que nous allons devenir n’a pas encore été montré.

es.L: Amados, ahora somos hijos de Dios, y todavía no se ha manifestado lo que seremos.
es.B: Queridos amigos, ya ahora somos hijos de Dios, y lo que seremos aún no se ha manifestado.
es.R: Queridos amigos, ahora mismo somos hijos de Dios. Pero lo que vamos a ser todavía no se ha mostrado.

sw.L: Wapendwa, sasa sisi ni watoto wa Mungu, na kile tutakachokuwa bado hakijadhihirishwa.
sw.B: Rafiki zangu wapendwa, sisi ni watoto wa Mungu sasa, na kile tutakachokuwa bado hakijadhihirishwa.
sw.R: Rafiki zangu wapendwa, sisi ni watoto wa Mungu hata sasa. Lakini bado haijaonyeshwa tutakavyokuwa baadaye.

ko.L: 사랑하는 여러분, 우리는 지금 하나님의 자녀입니다. 그리고 우리가 장차 어떻게 될지는 아직 나타나지 않았습니다.
ko.B: 사랑하는 여러분, 우리는 지금 하나님의 자녀입니다. 그러나 우리가 장차 어떻게 될지는 아직 드러나지 않았습니다.
ko.R: 사랑하는 여러분, 우리는 바로 지금 하나님의 자녀입니다. 그러나 우리가 앞으로 어떻게 될지는 아직 보이지 않았습니다.

decisions.choice: beloved: people loved, by God and by the writer
decisions.reason: ἀγαπητοί is the passive form of the word for love: "loved ones". It is the letter's warm way of addressing its readers (2:7; 4:1, 7, 11), and in this context it echoes the Father's love just described.

decisions.choice: now and not yet: being God's children is a present fact; what that will finally mean is still to be shown
decisions.reason: "Now" and "not yet" set the present beside the future. The readers already are God's children, but the full shape of that life waits for the time when Christ is revealed (2:28; 3:2b).

decisions.choice: revealed: brought out into the open, made visible
decisions.reason: φανερόω is a key verb in this letter: the life was revealed (1:2), Christ will be revealed at his coming (2:28; 3:2b), he was revealed to take away sins (3:5, 3:8). The future is not undecided; it is simply not yet visible.

decisions.choice: Dear friends (Balanced, Readable); Beloved (Literal)
decisions.reason: "Beloved" now sounds old-fashioned outside church; "Dear friends" keeps the warmth of a direct address. Literal keeps "Beloved" so the link to the word love stays visible.

source.text: οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἐὰν φανερωθῇ ὅμοιοι αὐτῷ ἐσόμεθα, ὅτι ὀψόμεθα αὐτὸν καθώς ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: We know that if he is revealed, like him we will be, because we will see him just as he is.

en.L: We know that when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is revealed we will be like {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, because we will see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is.
en.B: What we do know is this: when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is revealed, we will be like {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, for we will see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} truly is.
en.R: We do know that when Jesus appears, we will be like {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, because we will see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} really is.

fr.L: Nous savons que, quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sera manifesté, nous serons semblables à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, parce que nous {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} verrons tel qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est.
fr.B: Ce que nous savons, c’est que, lorsqu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sera manifesté, nous serons semblables à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, car nous {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} verrons tel qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est vraiment.
fr.R: Nous savons que, quand Jésus paraîtra, nous serons comme {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, parce que nous {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} verrons tel qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est vraiment.

es.L: Sabemos que, cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se manifieste, seremos semejantes a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, porque {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} veremos tal como es.
es.B: Lo que sí sabemos es esto: cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se manifieste, seremos semejantes a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, porque {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} veremos tal como es en realidad.
es.R: Sí sabemos que, cuando Jesús aparezca, seremos como {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, porque {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} veremos tal como es de verdad.

sw.L: Tunajua kwamba atakapodhihirishwa tutakuwa kama {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, kwa sababu tutamwona jinsi {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alivyo.
sw.B: Lakini tunajua hili: atakapodhihirishwa, tutakuwa kama {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, kwa maana tutamwona jinsi {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alivyo hasa.
sw.R: Tunajua kwamba Yesu atakapotokea, tutafanana {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}, kwa sababu tutamwona jinsi {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alivyo kweli.

ko.L: 우리는 그분이 나타나시면 우리가 그분과 같아지리라는 것을 압니다. 우리가 그분을 계신 그대로 볼 것이기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 그러나 우리가 아는 것은 이것입니다. 그분이 나타나실 때에 우리는 그분과 같아질 것입니다. 우리가 그분을 참모습 그대로 볼 것이기 때문입니다.
ko.R: 그러나 우리는 예수님께서 나타나실 때 우리가 그분과 같아지리라는 것을 압니다. 우리가 그분을 있는 그대로 볼 것이기 때문입니다.

decisions.choice: the subject of "is revealed" is Christ, at his coming: when he is revealed we will be like him
alternatives: "when it is revealed": when what we will be is made known, we will be like him
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject. The previous clause used it of "what we will be", so "when it is revealed" is possible. But in 2:28 the same words, "if he is revealed", speak of Christ's coming, and "like him" and "see him" need a person to have been named. Christ is the one whose purity the next verse holds up (3:3).

decisions.choice: when: a future event that is certain, not a doubtful condition
decisions.reason: ἐὰν with this form of the verb can mean "when" for something expected to happen (John 12:32; 14:3). The writer does not doubt Christ's coming; the point is what will follow it.

decisions.choice: seeing him as he is will make us like him
alternatives: we will be like him, and that is why we will be able to see him
decisions.reason: ὅτι gives the reason for becoming like him: the sight of him will change those who see him (2 Corinthians 3:18). The other reading, that only those made like him can see him (Matthew 5:8), takes the clause backwards from its plain order.

decisions.choice: Jesus appears
decisions.reason: Readable names the person, following the meaning decision on the subject, and uses "appears", the everyday word for someone coming into view.

decisions.choice: atakapodhihirishwa (when he is revealed)
decisions.reason: The Greek "if" here points to a future event that is certain (m2). "-taka-" (when) says that in Swahili; "aki-" could sound like a doubtful condition. The subject is Christ at his coming (m1), named "Yesu" at Readable, as in the English Readable.

decisions.choice: "그분이 나타나시면" (L), "나타나실 때에" (B, R), with the honorific
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the subject of "is revealed" as Christ at his coming, and footnotes the reading "when it is revealed", meaning what we will be. Korean must choose, and the honorific "-시-" follows the meaning decision.

source.text: καὶ πᾶς ὁ ἔχων τὴν ἐλπίδα ταύτην ἐπ’ αὐτῷ ἁγνίζει ἑαυτὸν καθὼς ἐκεῖνος ἁγνός ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: And everyone having the hope this on him purifies himself, just as that one pure is.

en.L: And everyone who has this hope [set] on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} purifies {{gender:themselves|himself}}, just as that one is pure.
en.B: Everyone whose hope is set on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in this way makes {{gender:themselves|himself}} pure, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is pure.
en.R: Everyone who has this hope in Jesus keeps {{gender:their|his}} life pure, just as Jesus is pure.

fr.L: Et quiconque a cette espérance [placée] en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} se purifie lui-même, comme celui-là est pur.
fr.B: Quiconque a mis en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} une telle espérance se rend pur, comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est pur.
fr.R: Celui qui espère ainsi en Jésus garde sa vie pure, comme Jésus est pur.

es.L: Y todo el que tiene esta esperanza [puesta] en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se purifica, así como aquel es puro.
es.B: Todo el que tiene así su esperanza puesta en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se purifica, así como {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es puro.
es.R: Todo el que tiene esta esperanza en Jesús mantiene pura su vida, así como Jesús es puro.

sw.L: Na kila aliye na tumaini hili {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} anajitakasa, kama vile yule alivyo safi.
sw.B: Kila aliye na tumaini hili {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} anajiweka safi, kama {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alivyo safi.
sw.R: Kila mtu aliye na tumaini hili kwa Yesu anaendelea kuishi maisha safi, kama Yesu alivyo safi.

ko.L: 그분께 이 소망을 두는 사람은 누구나, 그분이 깨끗하신 것처럼 자기를 깨끗하게 합니다.
ko.B: 그분께 이런 소망을 두는 사람은 누구나, 그분이 깨끗하신 것처럼 자기를 깨끗하게 합니다.
ko.R: 예수님께 이런 소망을 두는 사람은 누구나, 예수님께서 깨끗하신 것처럼 자기의 삶을 깨끗하게 지킵니다.

decisions.choice: hope set on him: the hope rests on Christ
decisions.reason: The preposition with the dative describes what the hope rests on (Romans 15:12; 1 Timothy 4:10). The pronoun is Christ, the one who will be revealed (3:2).

decisions.choice: that one: Christ
decisions.reason: ἐκεῖνος ("that one") is the letter's regular way of pointing to Christ (2:6; 3:5, 7, 16; 4:17), set apart from the ordinary pronoun used in the same sentences.

decisions.choice: purify oneself: to make one's life clean, morally pure
decisions.reason: ἁγνίζω is used of the ritual cleansing before a festival (John 11:55; Acts 21:24), but here it describes the way of life of someone waiting to meet Christ. The present tense shows an ongoing effort, not a single act.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Christ for the pronoun and for "that one", following the meaning decisions on both, and says "keeps their life pure" for the ongoing sense of the verb.

decisions.choice: se purifica; su vida, no gender span
decisions.reason: Spanish "se purifica" and "su vida" do not mark gender, so the English spans "themselves|himself" and "their|his" need no counterpart. "Aquel" for Christ is a demonstrative, like the English "that one", and takes no deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: anajitakasa ... safi (L); anajiweka safi ... safi (B); kuishi maisha safi ... safi (R)
decisions.reason: To purify oneself is to make one's life morally clean (m3). Literal uses "kujitakasa", as 1 Peter 1:22 does for the same verb; Balanced and Readable say "safi" (pure) in both halves, so the reader hears that the believer's purity follows Christ's, as the Greek uses one root for both.

source.text: Πᾶς ὁ ποιῶν τὴν ἁμαρτίαν καὶ τὴν ἀνομίαν ποιεῖ, καὶ ἡ ἁμαρτία ἐστὶν ἡ ἀνομία.

records.literal_gloss: Everyone doing the sin also the lawlessness does, and the sin is the lawlessness.

en.L: Everyone who does sin also does lawlessness, and sin is lawlessness.
en.B: Everyone who goes on sinning is also practicing lawlessness; sin is lawlessness.
en.R: Everyone who keeps on sinning is rebelling against God's law. That is what sin is: rebellion against God's law.

fr.L: Quiconque fait le péché fait aussi l’iniquité, et le péché est l’iniquité.
fr.B: Quiconque continue à pécher pratique aussi l’iniquité : le péché, c’est l’iniquité.
fr.R: Celui qui continue à pécher se révolte contre la loi de Dieu. C’est cela, le péché : se révolter contre la loi de Dieu.

es.L: Todo el que practica el pecado practica también la iniquidad, y el pecado es la iniquidad.
es.B: Todo el que sigue pecando practica también la rebeldía contra Dios; el pecado es rebeldía contra Dios.
es.R: Todo el que sigue pecando se está rebelando contra la ley de Dios. Eso es el pecado: rebelarse contra la ley de Dios.

sw.L: Kila anayeifanya dhambi anaufanya pia uasi; na dhambi ndiyo uasi.
sw.B: Kila anayeendelea kutenda dhambi anafanya uasi pia; dhambi ni uasi.
sw.R: Kila anayeendelea kutenda dhambi anaiasi sheria ya Mungu. Hivyo ndivyo dhambi ilivyo: kuiasi sheria ya Mungu.

ko.L: 죄를 행하는 사람은 누구나 불법도 행합니다. 죄는 불법입니다.
ko.B: 계속 죄를 짓는 사람은 누구나 불법을 행하는 것입니다. 죄는 곧 불법입니다.
ko.R: 계속 죄를 짓는 사람은 누구나 하나님의 법을 거역하는 것입니다. 죄가 바로 그것, 곧 하나님의 법을 거역하는 것입니다.

decisions.choice: doing sin: sin as a practice, a way of life
decisions.reason: The present participle of ποιέω with "the sin" describes what someone habitually does, as in John 8:34 ("everyone who does sin is a slave of sin") and 3:8 below. The letter has already said that believers do commit sins and must confess them (1:8-2:1); see the decision at 3:6.

decisions.choice: lawlessness: defiance of God's will, rebellion against his rule
alternatives: breaking the commandments of the law of Moses
decisions.reason: ἀνομία is not simply breaking a rule. It is living as if God's law did not apply, the attitude of the last days (Matthew 24:12; 2 Thessalonians 2:3-8). The letter has just spoken of the last hour and the antichrists (2:18), and some taught that sin did not matter (3:7); the writer answers that sin is rebellion against God.

decisions.choice: sin and lawlessness are the same thing
alternatives: sin is a kind of lawlessness
decisions.reason: Both nouns have the article, so the sentence says the two can be exchanged: there is no sin that is not rebellion against God.

decisions.choice: goes on sinning (Balanced); keeps on sinning (Readable)
decisions.reason: The same words as John 8:34, where Balanced says "goes on sinning" and Readable "keeps on sinning"; they carry the meaning decision on the present tense. Literal keeps "does sin".

decisions.choice: rebelling against God's law; rebellion against God's law
decisions.reason: "Lawlessness" is a hard word for young readers, and "breaking the law" is too weak: it would make sin a legal slip. Readable says what the word means in this passage, following the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: l’iniquité (L, B); se révolter contre la loi de Dieu (R)
decisions.reason: The word is defiance of God's will, not a legal slip (m2). "Illégalité" and "transgression de la loi" would make it a breach of rules; "iniquité" is the established French word for wickedness against God's order and is kept at Literal and Balanced, as the English keeps "lawlessness". Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does. "Continue à pécher" (B, R) as in John 8:34.

decisions.choice: iniquidad (L); rebeldía contra Dios (B); rebelarse contra la ley de Dios (R)
decisions.reason: The word means defiance of God's will (meaning decision m1). Literal uses "iniquidad", as elsewhere in the New Testament drafts; "maldad" would be too general here, so Balanced says what kind of wrong it is, and Readable follows the English Readable.

decisions.choice: uasi (L, B); kuiasi sheria ya Mungu (R)
decisions.reason: The word is defiance of God's will, rebellion against his rule (m2). "Uasi" (rebellion) says that, as in the project's other New Testament books; Readable says "rebelling against God's law", as the English Readable does. "Maovu" (wickedness) would lose the rebellion.

decisions.choice: "불법" (L, B); "하나님의 법을 거역하는 것" (R)
decisions.reason: Lawlessness is defiance of God's will, rebellion against his rule (meaning decision). "불법" is the plain word; Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ οἴδατε ὅτι ἐκεῖνος ἐφανερώθη ἵνα τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἄρῃ, καὶ ἁμαρτία ἐν αὐτῷ οὐκ ἔστιν.

records.literal_gloss: And you know that that one was revealed in order that the sins he might take away, and sin in him not is.

en.L: And you know that that one was revealed in order that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might take away the sins, and in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} there is no sin.
en.B: You know that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was revealed so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could take sins away, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has no sin in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: You know that Jesus came to take away sins. And there is no sin in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

fr.L: Et vous savez que celui-là a été manifesté afin qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} enlève les péchés, et il n’y a pas de péché en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Vous savez qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a été manifesté pour enlever les péchés, et il n’y a pas de péché en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Vous savez que Jésus est venu pour enlever les péchés. Et il n’y a aucun péché en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} que aquel se manifestó para quitar los pecados, y en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} no hay pecado.
es.B: {{plural_you:Ustedes saben|Vosotros sabéis}} que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se manifestó para quitar los pecados, y en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} no hay pecado.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes saben|Vosotros sabéis}} que Jesús vino para quitar los pecados. Y en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} no hay pecado.

sw.L: Na mnafahamu kwamba yule alidhihirishwa ili aziondoe zile dhambi, na dhambi hakuna ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.B: Mnajua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alidhihirishwa ili aziondoe dhambi, na ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} hamna dhambi.
sw.R: Mnajua kwamba Yesu alikuja ili aziondoe dhambi. Na ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} hamna dhambi yoyote.

ko.L: 그리고 여러분은 그분이 죄를 없애시려고 나타나셨다는 것을 압니다. 그분 안에는 죄가 없습니다.
ko.B: 여러분이 알다시피, 그분은 죄를 없애시려고 나타나셨습니다. 그리고 그분 안에는 죄가 없습니다.
ko.R: 여러분은 예수님께서 죄를 없애시려고 오셨다는 것을 압니다. 그리고 그분 안에는 죄가 하나도 없습니다.

decisions.choice: was revealed: Christ's first coming, when he came into the world as a man
decisions.reason: The past tense looks back, as in 1:2 ("the life was revealed"), while 2:28 and 3:2 look forward to his coming again. The same verb ties the two comings together.

decisions.choice: take away sins: echoes John the Baptist's words about the Lamb of God
decisions.reason: John 1:29 calls Jesus "the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world", with the same verb. Behind both stands Isaiah 53, the servant who bears the sins of many.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "the sins"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "our sins", which may have come in from 2:2 or 4:10; some important early manuscripts have the shorter text, which SBLGNT follows. The meaning hardly changes. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: Christ is without sin
decisions.reason: The present tense states what is always true of him (John 8:46; 2 Corinthians 5:21; Hebrews 4:15). The one who came to remove sin had none of his own, which is why he can take it away and why sin has no place in those who remain in him (3:6).

decisions.choice: Jesus came
decisions.reason: Readable names Christ and says plainly what "was revealed" means here, following the meaning decision: his coming into the world.

decisions.choice: aziondoe dhambi
decisions.reason: The words echo John the Baptist's words about the Lamb of God (m2), and "kuondoa" is the verb used in John 1:29, so the echo stays.

source.text: πᾶς ὁ ἐν αὐτῷ μένων οὐχ ἁμαρτάνει· πᾶς ὁ ἁμαρτάνων οὐχ ἑώρακεν αὐτὸν οὐδὲ ἔγνωκεν αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: Everyone in him remaining not sins; everyone sinning not has seen him nor has known him.

en.L: Everyone who remains in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} does not sin; everyone who sins has not seen {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} nor known {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Whoever remains in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} does not go on sinning; whoever goes on sinning has neither seen {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} nor come to know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Anyone who remains in Jesus does not keep on sinning. Anyone who keeps on sinning has never seen {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} or known {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

fr.L: Quiconque demeure en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ne pèche pas ; quiconque pèche ne {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a pas vu et ne {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a pas connu.
fr.B: Celui qui demeure en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ne continue pas à pécher ; celui qui continue à pécher ne {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a ni vu ni connu.
fr.R: Celui qui demeure en Jésus ne continue pas à pécher. Celui qui continue à pécher ne {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a jamais vu et ne {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a jamais connu.

es.L: Todo el que permanece en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} no peca; todo el que peca no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} ha visto ni {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} ha conocido.
es.B: Quien permanece en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} no sigue pecando; quien sigue pecando no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} ha visto ni {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} ha llegado a conocer.
es.R: Quien permanece en Jesús no sigue pecando. Quien sigue pecando nunca {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} ha visto ni {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} ha conocido.

sw.L: Kila anayekaa ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} hatendi dhambi; kila anayetenda dhambi hajamwona wala hajamfahamu.
sw.B: Yeyote anayekaa ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} haendelei kutenda dhambi; yeyote anayeendelea kutenda dhambi hajamwona wala hajamjua.
sw.R: Mtu anayekaa ndani ya Yesu haendelei kutenda dhambi. Mtu anayeendelea kutenda dhambi hajawahi kumwona wala kumjua.

ko.L: 그분 안에 머무는 사람은 누구나 죄를 짓지 않습니다. 죄를 짓는 사람은 누구나 그분을 보지도 못했고 알지도 못했습니다.
ko.B: 그분 안에 머물러 있는 사람은 계속 죄를 짓지 않습니다. 계속 죄를 짓는 사람은 그분을 본 적도 없고 알지도 못합니다.
ko.R: 예수님 안에 머물러 있는 사람은 계속 죄를 짓지 않습니다. 계속 죄를 짓는 사람은 그분을 본 적도 없고 그분을 알지도 못합니다.

decisions.choice: the present tense describes a settled way of life: whoever remains in him does not go on sinning
alternatives: whoever remains in him never commits any sin at all
the verse describes the new life as it is in itself, an ideal not yet fully seen in believers
a particular sin is meant, such as the lawlessness of 3:4 or the sin that leads to death (5:16)
decisions.reason: ἁμαρτάνει and ἁμαρτάνων are present tense, which often describes what someone does as a habit or as their character. In 2:1 the letter uses a different tense for a single act ("if anyone does sin, we have an advocate"). But the present tense can also state a general truth without stressing habit, so the grammar alone does not settle it; the reading rests on the context, which is why it is marked uncertain.

decisions.choice: the verse does not teach that believers are sinless; it denies that sin can be the pattern of a life joined to Christ
alternatives: believers who remain in Christ live without sin
decisions.reason: The same letter says that anyone who claims to have no sin deceives themselves (1:8, 1:10), urges confession (1:9), and promises an advocate for the one who sins (2:1). Both must stand together. The writer is answering those who said sin did not matter (3:7): a person who goes on sinning untroubled shows that they do not know Christ at all. Some read the two sets of verses as describing the ideal and the reality of Christian life; they are both meant seriously.

decisions.choice: remain in him: live in lasting union with Christ
decisions.reason: μένω is a favourite word of this letter and of John's Gospel for a relationship that continues (John 15:4-7; 1 John 2:6, 2:24, 2:27-28).

decisions.choice: seen and known him: spiritual perception and personal knowledge of Christ
decisions.reason: The readers had not seen Jesus in the flesh, so seeing here is the sight of faith, as in 3 John 11 and John 14:7-9. The two perfect tenses describe a seeing and knowing that has lasting effect.

decisions.choice: go on sinning (Balanced); keep on sinning (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the meaning decision on the present tense into words; Literal keeps the bare "does not sin" so a reader can see the Greek as it stands. A footnote gives the other readings.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Christ, the one just described in 3:5.

decisions.choice: haendelei kutenda dhambi; anayeendelea kutenda dhambi
decisions.reason: The present tense describes a settled way of life (m1); the verse does not say believers never sin (m2). Balanced and Readable say "does not go on sinning" with "kuendelea", as 5:18 does, and Literal keeps the plain present.

decisions.choice: "계속 죄를 짓다" (B, R), here and in 3:8-9; "죄를 짓다" (L)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the present tense as a settled way of life, and footnotes it: the verse does not teach that believers are sinless. Balanced and Readable add "계속", as the English adds "go on" and "keep on"; Literal keeps the bare verb.

source.text: τεκνία, μηδεὶς πλανάτω ὑμᾶς· ὁ ποιῶν τὴν δικαιοσύνην δίκαιός ἐστιν, καθὼς ἐκεῖνος δίκαιός ἐστιν·

records.literal_gloss: Little children, no one let lead astray you; the one doing the righteousness righteous is, just as that one righteous is;

en.L: Little children, let no one lead you astray; the one who does righteousness is righteous, just as that one is righteous.
en.B: Dear children, do not let anyone mislead you: it is the person who practices righteousness who is righteous, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is righteous.
en.R: Dear children, do not let anyone fool you. People who live a righteous life are righteous, just as Jesus is righteous.

fr.L: Petits enfants, que personne ne vous égare : celui qui pratique la justice est juste, comme celui-là est juste.
fr.B: Mes chers enfants, ne laissez personne vous égarer : c’est celui qui fait ce qui est juste qui est juste, comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est juste.
fr.R: Mes chers enfants, ne laissez personne vous tromper. Ceux qui vivent d’une manière juste sont justes, comme Jésus est juste.

es.L: Hijitos, que nadie {{plural_you:los|os}} extravíe; el que practica la justicia es justo, así como aquel es justo.
es.B: Hijitos, no {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} que nadie {{plural_you:los|os}} engañe: quien practica la justicia es justo, así como {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es justo.
es.R: Hijos queridos, no {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} que nadie {{plural_you:los|os}} engañe. Las personas que llevan una vida justa son justas, así como Jesús es justo.

sw.L: Watoto wadogo, mtu yeyote asiwapotoshe: anayeitenda haki ni mwenye haki, sawa na yule alivyo mwenye haki.
sw.B: Wanangu wapendwa, msikubali mtu yeyote awapotoshe: mtu anayetenda haki ndiye mwenye haki, kama {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alivyo mwenye haki.
sw.R: Wanangu wapendwa, msikubali mtu yeyote awadanganye. Watu wanaoishi maisha ya haki ni wenye haki, kama Yesu alivyo mwenye haki.

ko.L: 어린 자녀 여러분, 아무에게도 미혹되지 마십시오. 의를 행하는 사람은 그분이 의로우신 것처럼 의롭습니다.
ko.B: 어린 자녀 여러분, 아무에게도 속지 마십시오. 의를 행하는 사람이 바로 의로운 사람입니다. 그분이 의로우신 것과 같습니다.
ko.R: 사랑하는 자녀 여러분, 아무에게도 속지 마십시오. 의롭게 사는 사람들은 예수님께서 의로우신 것처럼 의롭습니다.

decisions.choice: lead astray: deceive, draw away from the truth
decisions.reason: πλανάω is the word the letter uses for the false teachers (2:26; 1:8). The warning suggests some were teaching that a person could be right with God while living in sin.

decisions.choice: doing what is right shows who is righteous; it does not make a person righteous
decisions.reason: The parallel in 2:29 says that everyone who does righteousness "has been born of him": the conduct is the evidence of the new birth, not its cause. The point is against those who claimed to be righteous without living rightly.

decisions.choice: that one: Christ, the Righteous One
decisions.reason: As in 3:3 and 3:5, "that one" is Christ. He is "Jesus Christ the righteous" in 2:1.

decisions.choice: Little children (Literal); Dear children (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: τεκνίον is a diminutive of the word for child, a term of affection from an older pastor (2:1, 2:12, 2:28). Balanced and Readable say it in everyday words, as the other chapters do.

decisions.choice: Jesus; live a righteous life
decisions.reason: Readable names Christ, following the meaning decision, and puts "does righteousness" as a way of living, keeping the key word.

source.text: ὁ ποιῶν τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ἐκ τοῦ διαβόλου ἐστίν, ὅτι ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς ὁ διάβολος ἁμαρτάνει.

records.literal_gloss: The one doing the sin of the devil is, because from beginning the devil sins.

en.L: The one who does sin is of the devil, because from [the] beginning the devil sins.
en.B: Whoever goes on sinning belongs to the devil, because the devil has sinned from the beginning and has never stopped.
en.R: Anyone who keeps on sinning belongs to the devil, because the devil has been sinning since the very beginning.

fr.L: Celui qui fait le péché est du diable, car depuis le commencement le diable pèche.
fr.B: Celui qui continue à pécher appartient au diable, car le diable pèche depuis le commencement et n’a jamais cessé.
fr.R: Celui qui continue à pécher appartient au diable, parce que le diable pèche depuis le tout début.

es.L: El que practica el pecado es del diablo, porque desde [el] principio el diablo peca.
es.B: Quien sigue pecando pertenece al diablo, porque el diablo ha pecado desde el principio y nunca ha dejado de hacerlo.
es.R: Quien sigue pecando pertenece al diablo, porque el diablo ha estado pecando desde el mismo principio.

sw.L: Yule anayetenda dhambi ni wa Ibilisi, kwa kuwa tangu mwanzo Ibilisi anatenda dhambi.
sw.B: Yeyote anayeendelea kutenda dhambi ni wa Ibilisi, kwa sababu Ibilisi amekuwa akitenda dhambi tangu mwanzo, wala hajaacha.
sw.R: Mtu anayeendelea kutenda dhambi ni wa Ibilisi, kwa sababu Ibilisi amekuwa akitenda dhambi tangu mwanzo kabisa.

ko.L: 죄를 행하는 사람은 마귀에게 속해 있습니다. 마귀는 처음부터 죄를 짓고 있기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 계속 죄를 짓는 사람은 마귀에게 속한 사람입니다. 마귀는 처음부터 죄를 지어 왔고, 지금도 멈추지 않았기 때문입니다.
ko.R: 계속 죄를 짓는 사람은 마귀에게 속한 사람입니다. 마귀는 맨 처음부터 죄를 지어 왔기 때문입니다.

decisions.choice: of the devil: belonging to him, sharing his character as a child shares a parent's
decisions.reason: The phrase describes where a person comes from and whom they resemble, as "born of God" does in 3:9. Verse 10 speaks of "the children of the devil", and Jesus uses the same picture in John 8:44.

decisions.choice: from the beginning the devil has been sinning, and still is
alternatives: the devil sinned once, at the beginning
decisions.reason: The present tense with "from the beginning" describes something that started then and goes on now. The beginning is the start of the human story, when the serpent led the first people into sin (Genesis 3; John 8:44, "a murderer from the beginning").

decisions.choice: has sinned from the beginning and has never stopped
alternatives: has been sinning from the beginning
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the two parts of the meaning decision on the tense, past start and present continuation, in plain words. Readable says "has been sinning since", which carries the same sense.

decisions.choice: Ibilisi
decisions.reason: The Greek word here is "devil", and "Ibilisi" is the Swahili word for it, as in the Gospels; "Shetani" is kept for the name Satan. "Ni wa Ibilisi" (is of the devil) says that the person belongs to him and shares his character (m1).

decisions.choice: "마귀" for the devil at every level (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: "마귀" is the established Protestant word, as in the Korean John 8:44 and James 4:7.

source.text: εἰς τοῦτο ἐφανερώθη ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ ἵνα λύσῃ τὰ ἔργα τοῦ διαβόλου.

records.literal_gloss: For this was revealed the Son of the God, that he might undo the works of the devil.

en.L: For this [purpose] the Son of God was revealed: that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might undo the works of the devil.
en.B: This is why the Son of God was revealed: to undo the works of the devil.
en.R: The Son of God came for this very reason: to undo what the devil has done.

fr.L: Pour ceci le Fils de Dieu a été manifesté : afin qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} défasse les œuvres du diable.
fr.B: Voici pourquoi le Fils de Dieu a été manifesté : pour défaire les œuvres du diable.
fr.R: Le Fils de Dieu est venu justement pour cela : pour défaire ce que le diable a fait.

es.L: Para esto se manifestó el Hijo de Dios: para deshacer las obras del diablo.
es.B: Por eso se manifestó el Hijo de Dios: para deshacer las obras del diablo.
es.R: El Hijo de Dios vino precisamente para esto: para deshacer lo que el diablo ha hecho.

sw.L: Kwa ajili ya hili Mwana wa Mungu alidhihirishwa, ili azibomoe kazi za Ibilisi.
sw.B: Hii ndiyo sababu Mwana wa Mungu alidhihirishwa: ili azibomoe kazi za Ibilisi.
sw.R: Mwana wa Mungu alikuja kwa sababu hii hasa: kuharibu yale ambayo Ibilisi ameyafanya.

ko.L: 이것을 위해 하나님의 아들이 나타나셨습니다. 곧 마귀의 일들을 허물어뜨리시려는 것입니다.
ko.B: 하나님의 아들이 나타나신 것은 바로 마귀가 한 일들을 허물어뜨리시려는 것입니다.
ko.R: 하나님의 아들께서는 바로 이 일 때문에 오셨습니다. 마귀가 한 일을 다 무너뜨리시려는 것입니다.

decisions.choice: for this purpose ... that: the second clause states the purpose announced by the first
decisions.reason: "For this" points forward to the ἵνα clause, as in 3:1. The sentence repeats the thought of 3:5 in the language of the conflict with the devil.

decisions.choice: undo: break up, dismantle, bring to nothing
decisions.reason: λύω means to loosen or untie, and from that to break down or do away with something (John 2:19, "destroy this temple"). Here it is the undoing of what the devil has built.

decisions.choice: the works of the devil: sin and all that comes from it, lies, hatred and death
decisions.reason: The letter names what the devil does: he has sinned from the beginning (3:8a), and Cain, who belonged to him, killed his brother (3:12). Jesus calls him a murderer and a liar (John 8:44).

decisions.choice: came
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "was revealed" means here, his coming into the world, as at 3:5.

decisions.choice: défaire
decisions.reason: The verb means to break up and bring to nothing what has been built (m2). "Défaire" says it as the English "undo" does; "détruire" would suggest only violence.

decisions.choice: azibomoe (L, B); kuharibu (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is to break up, dismantle and bring to nothing (m2). "Kubomoa" (pull down, demolish) gives that picture; Readable uses the plainer "kuharibu" (destroy, undo).

source.text: πᾶς ὁ γεγεννημένος ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ ἁμαρτίαν οὐ ποιεῖ, ὅτι σπέρμα αὐτοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ μένει, καὶ οὐ δύναται ἁμαρτάνειν, ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ γεγέννηται.

records.literal_gloss: Everyone having been born of the God sin not does, because seed of him in him remains, and not he is able to sin, because of the God he has been born.

en.L: Everyone who has been born of God does not do sin, because {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} seed remains in {{gender:them|him}}; and {{gender:they are|he is}} not able to sin, because {{gender:they have|he has}} been born of God.
en.B: Whoever has been born of God does not go on sinning, for God's seed remains in {{gender:them|him}}; {{gender:they are|he is}} not able to go on sinning, because it is from God that {{gender:they have|he has}} been born.
en.R: People who are born of God do not keep on sinning. God's own life is in them like a seed, and it stays there. They cannot keep on sinning, because God is the one who gave them new birth.

fr.L: Quiconque est né de Dieu ne fait pas le péché, parce que {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} semence demeure en lui ; et il ne peut pas pécher, parce qu’il est né de Dieu.
fr.B: Celui qui est né de Dieu ne continue pas à pécher, car la semence de Dieu demeure en lui ; il ne peut pas continuer à pécher, puisque c’est de Dieu qu’il est né.
fr.R: Ceux qui sont nés de Dieu ne continuent pas à pécher. La vie même de Dieu est en eux comme une semence, et elle y reste. Ils ne peuvent pas continuer à pécher, parce que c’est Dieu qui les a fait naître à une vie nouvelle.

es.L: Todo el que ha nacido de Dios no practica el pecado, porque {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} semilla permanece en {{gender:esa persona|él}}; y no puede pecar, porque ha nacido de Dios.
es.B: Quien ha nacido de Dios no sigue pecando, porque la semilla de Dios permanece en {{gender:esa persona|él}}; no puede seguir pecando, porque ha nacido de Dios.
es.R: Las personas que han nacido de Dios no siguen pecando. La vida misma de Dios está en ellas como una semilla, y se queda allí. No pueden seguir pecando, porque Dios es quien les dio una vida nueva.

sw.L: Kila aliyezaliwa kutoka kwa Mungu hatendi dhambi, kwa kuwa mbegu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} inakaa ndani yake; naye hawezi kutenda dhambi, kwa kuwa amezaliwa kutoka kwa Mungu.
sw.B: Yeyote aliyezaliwa na Mungu haendelei kutenda dhambi, kwa maana mbegu ya Mungu inakaa ndani yake; hawezi kuendelea kutenda dhambi, kwa sababu amezaliwa na Mungu.
sw.R: Watu waliozaliwa na Mungu hawaendelei kutenda dhambi. Uzima wa Mungu mwenyewe uko ndani yao kama mbegu, nao unakaa humo. Hawawezi kuendelea kutenda dhambi, kwa sababu Mungu ndiye aliyewapa kuzaliwa upya.

ko.L: 하나님에게서 난 사람은 누구나 죄를 행하지 않습니다. 하나님의 씨가 그 사람 안에 머물기 때문입니다. 그리고 그는 죄를 지을 수 없습니다. 하나님에게서 났기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 하나님에게서 태어난 사람은 계속 죄를 짓지 않습니다. 하나님의 씨가 그 사람 안에 머물러 있기 때문입니다. 그는 계속 죄를 지을 수 없습니다. 하나님에게서 태어났기 때문입니다.
ko.R: 하나님에게서 태어난 사람들은 계속 죄를 짓지 않습니다. 하나님 자신의 생명이 씨처럼 그들 안에 있고, 그 생명이 그 안에 머물러 있습니다. 그들은 계속 죄를 지을 수 없습니다. 하나님께서 그들을 새로 태어나게 하셨기 때문입니다.

decisions.choice: the present tense describes a way of life: the one born of God does not go on sinning and cannot go on sinning
alternatives: the one born of God never commits any sin and is incapable of it
the verse describes the new life in itself, an ideal not yet fully seen
a particular sin is meant, such as the lawlessness of 3:4 or the sin that leads to death (5:16)
decisions.reason: ποιεῖ is present tense and ἁμαρτάνειν a present infinitive, the tense of continuing action. Read that way, the verse says that sinning cannot be the settled pattern of someone born of God, as at 3:6. The present tense does not always stress habit, so the grammar alone does not decide the question; it is marked uncertain for that reason.

decisions.choice: new birth makes a life given over to sin impossible; it does not make a believer unable ever to sin
alternatives: those born of God are made incapable of sinning at all
decisions.reason: The letter itself says that believers sin and must confess it (1:8-10), promises an advocate when they do (2:1), and tells them to pray for a brother or sister who sins (5:16). "Cannot" therefore describes what the new nature is like: a child of God cannot live at home in sin, because God's own life is at work in them.

decisions.choice: his seed: the life God plants in those he gives birth to, by which they come to share his nature
alternatives: God's word, planted in them (1 Peter 1:23; James 1:18)
"his offspring": God's children remain in God
decisions.reason: σπέρμα carries on the picture of being born of God: as a child shares the life of the one who fathered it, so the one born of God carries God's life within. The letter does not say whether that life is given through the word (2:14, "the word of God remains in you") or the Spirit (3:24), and both may be in view. The reading "his offspring remain in him" is grammatically possible but turns the pronouns around against the flow of the verse.

decisions.choice: his = God's; in him = in the one born of God
decisions.reason: The first pronoun points back to God named just before; the second to the person born of him, the subject of the sentence.

decisions.choice: does not go on sinning; not able to go on sinning (Balanced); do not keep on sinning; cannot keep on sinning (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the meaning decision on the present tense into words, as at 3:6; Literal keeps "does not do sin" and "not able to sin".

decisions.choice: God's seed (Balanced); God's own life is in them like a seed (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced names God as the owner of the seed so the pronouns are clear. Readable explains the picture without choosing between the word and the Spirit, following the meaning decision; it goes beyond the bare words, so reviewers should weigh it.

decisions.choice: semilla
decisions.reason: "Semilla" is the everyday word and keeps the picture of life planted to grow (meaning decision m2); "simiente" is old-fashioned. "No puede pecar" does not mark gender, so the English spans "they are|he is" need no counterpart.

decisions.choice: mbegu yake (L); mbegu ya Mungu (B); uzima wa Mungu ... kama mbegu (R)
decisions.reason: His seed is the life God plants in those he gives birth to (m3). "Mbegu" keeps the picture, as 1 Peter 1:23 does; "uzao" (offspring) would read as descendants. Readable explains it, as the English Readable does, with "uzima", the word for God's life.

decisions.choice: mbegu yake ... ndani yake
alternatives: mbegu yake ... ndani ya mtu huyo
decisions.reason: "His" is God's, and "in him" is the one born of God (m4). Literal spans only the first "yake", which means God; the second means the believer and takes no span.

decisions.choice: "하나님의 씨" (L, B); "하나님 자신의 생명이 씨처럼" (R)
decisions.reason: His seed is the life God plants in those he gives birth to (meaning decision, footnoted). Korean "그의" would be read as the person's own; the meaning decision says "his" is God's, so Literal and Balanced name God, and Readable explains the picture, as the English Readable does.

source.text: ἐν τούτῳ φανερά ἐστιν τὰ τέκνα τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τὰ τέκνα τοῦ διαβόλου· πᾶς ὁ μὴ ποιῶν δικαιοσύνην οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ ὁ μὴ ἀγαπῶν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: By this evident are the children of the God and the children of the devil: everyone not doing righteousness not is of the God, and the [one] not loving the brother of him.

en.L: By this the children of God and the children of the devil are evident: everyone who does not do righteousness is not of God, and [neither is] the one who does not love {{gender:their brother or sister|his brother}}.
en.B: This is how it becomes clear who are God's children and who are the devil's children: anyone who does not practice righteousness is not from God, and neither is anyone who does not love {{gender:their brother or sister|his brother}}.
en.R: Here is how you can tell who are God's children and who are the devil's children. Anyone who does not live a righteous life does not belong to God. And anyone who does not love a fellow believer does not belong to God either.

fr.L: À ceci sont manifestes les enfants de Dieu et les enfants du diable : quiconque ne pratique pas la justice n’est pas de Dieu, ni celui qui n’aime pas {{gender:son frère ou sa sœur|son frère}}.
fr.B: Voici à quoi l’on reconnaît les enfants de Dieu et les enfants du diable : quiconque ne fait pas ce qui est juste n’est pas de Dieu, pas plus que celui qui n’aime pas {{gender:son frère ou sa sœur|son frère}}.
fr.R: Voici comment on peut reconnaître qui sont les enfants de Dieu et qui sont les enfants du diable. Celui qui ne vit pas d’une manière juste n’appartient pas à Dieu. Et celui qui n’aime pas un frère ou une sœur dans la foi n’appartient pas à Dieu non plus.

es.L: En esto se hacen evidentes los hijos de Dios y los hijos del diablo: todo el que no practica la justicia no es de Dios, ni [lo es] el que no ama a {{gender:su hermano o hermana|su hermano}}.
es.B: Así se hace evidente quiénes son los hijos de Dios y quiénes los hijos del diablo: el que no practica la justicia no es de Dios, ni tampoco el que no ama a {{gender:su hermano o hermana|su hermano}}.
es.R: Así se puede saber quiénes son hijos de Dios y quiénes son hijos del diablo. El que no lleva una vida justa no pertenece a Dios. Y el que no ama a {{gender:un hermano o una hermana en la fe|un hermano en la fe}} tampoco pertenece a Dios.

sw.L: Katika hili watoto wa Mungu na watoto wa Ibilisi wanaonekana wazi: kila asiyetenda haki si wa Mungu, wala [si wa Mungu] yule asiyempenda ndugu yake.
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo inavyojulikana wazi ni nani watoto wa Mungu na ni nani watoto wa Ibilisi: yeyote asiyetenda haki hatoki kwa Mungu, wala yeyote asiyempenda ndugu yake.
sw.R: Hivi ndivyo mnavyoweza kujua ni nani watoto wa Mungu na ni nani watoto wa Ibilisi. Mtu asiyeishi maisha ya haki si wa Mungu. Na mtu asiyempenda mwamini mwenzake si wa Mungu pia.

ko.L: 이것으로 하나님의 자녀들과 마귀의 자녀들이 드러납니다. 의를 행하지 않는 사람은 누구나 하나님에게서 난 사람이 아니고, 자기 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}를 사랑하지 않는 사람도 [그렇습니다].
ko.B: 이것으로 누가 하나님의 자녀이고 누가 마귀의 자녀인지 분명히 드러납니다. 의를 행하지 않는 사람은 하나님에게서 난 사람이 아니고, 자기 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}를 사랑하지 않는 사람도 마찬가지입니다.
ko.R: 누가 하나님의 자녀이고 누가 마귀의 자녀인지 알 수 있는 길이 여기 있습니다. 의롭게 살지 않는 사람은 하나님께 속한 사람이 아닙니다. 그리고 믿음의 식구를 사랑하지 않는 사람도 하나님께 속한 사람이 아닙니다.

decisions.choice: by this: points forward to the test given after it
decisions.reason: The words can look back to what has just been said about sin and new birth, but the clause after the raised dot spells out the test: doing what is right, and loving one's brother or sister. The two readings say the same thing.

decisions.choice: his brother: a fellow believer, man or woman
decisions.reason: In this letter the brother is a member of God's family (2:9-11; 3:14-17; 4:20-21). The masculine is the ordinary way of speaking of men and women together.

decisions.choice: love for fellow believers is named as the plainest form of doing right
decisions.reason: The added clause narrows the test: righteousness is seen above all in love. It opens the theme of the next verses (3:11-18).

decisions.choice: {{gender:their brother or sister|his brother}} (Literal, Balanced); a fellow believer (Readable)
decisions.reason: The gender setting gives the inclusive default and the traditional form. Readable says "a fellow believer", which is already inclusive and makes clear that a family member by birth is not meant.

decisions.choice: does not live a righteous life
alternatives: does not do what is right
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the key word righteous and puts "doing righteousness" as a way of living.

source.text: Ὅτι αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ ἀγγελία ἣν ἠκούσατε ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς, ἵνα ἀγαπῶμεν ἀλλήλους· οὐ καθὼς Κάϊν ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ ἦν καὶ ἔσφαξεν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ· καὶ χάριν τίνος ἔσφαξεν αὐτόν;

records.literal_gloss: Because this is the message which you heard from beginning, that we should love one another, \v 12 not as Cain of the evil [one] was and slaughtered the brother of him; and for the sake of what did he slaughter him?

en.L: For this is the message that you heard from [the] beginning: that we should love one another, \v 12 not as Cain [who] was of the evil one and slaughtered his brother. And why did he slaughter him?
en.B: For the message you heard from the beginning is this: we should love one another. \v 12 We must not be like Cain, who belonged to the evil one and murdered his brother. And why did he murder him?
en.R: From the very beginning you heard this message: we must love one another. \v 12 We must not be like Cain. He belonged to the evil one, the devil, and he killed his own brother. Why did he kill him?

fr.L: Car voici le message que vous avez entendu depuis le commencement : que nous nous aimions les uns les autres, \v 12 non comme Caïn, [qui] était du Mauvais et a égorgé son frère. Et pourquoi l’a-t-il égorgé ?
fr.B: Car le message que vous avez entendu depuis le commencement, le voici : nous devons nous aimer les uns les autres. \v 12 Ne soyons pas comme Caïn, qui appartenait au Mauvais et qui a assassiné son frère. Et pourquoi l’a-t-il assassiné ?
fr.R: Dès le tout début, vous avez entendu ce message : nous devons nous aimer les uns les autres. \v 12 Nous ne devons pas être comme Caïn. Il appartenait au Mauvais, le diable, et il a tué son propre frère. Pourquoi l’a-t-il tué ?

es.L: Porque este es el mensaje que {{plural_you:oyeron|oísteis}} desde [el] principio: que nos amemos unos a otros, \v 12 no como Caín, [que] era del maligno y degolló a su hermano. ¿Y por qué lo degolló?
es.B: Porque el mensaje que {{plural_you:oyeron|oísteis}} desde el principio es este: que nos amemos unos a otros. \v 12 No debemos ser como Caín, que pertenecía al maligno y asesinó a su hermano. ¿Y por qué lo asesinó?
es.R: Desde el mismo principio {{plural_you:oyeron|oísteis}} este mensaje: debemos amarnos unos a otros. \v 12 No debemos ser como Caín. Él pertenecía al maligno, el diablo, y mató a su propio hermano. ¿Por qué lo mató?

sw.L: Kwa kuwa huu ndio ujumbe ambao mmeusikia tangu mwanzo: tupendane sisi kwa sisi, \v 12 si kama Kaini [aliyekuwa] wa yule mwovu, akamchinja ndugu yake. Na kwa sababu gani alimchinja?
sw.B: Ujumbe mliousikia tangu mwanzo ni huu: tupendane. \v 12 Tusiwe kama Kaini, aliyekuwa wa yule mwovu, akamuua ndugu yake. Na kwa nini alimuua?
sw.R: Tangu mwanzo kabisa mlisikia ujumbe huu: lazima tupendane. \v 12 Tusiwe kama Kaini. Yeye alikuwa wa yule mwovu, yaani Ibilisi, na alimuua ndugu yake mwenyewe. Kwa nini alimuua?

ko.L: 여러분이 처음부터 들은 소식은 이것이기 때문입니다. 곧 우리가 서로 사랑해야 한다는 것입니다. \v 12 가인처럼 하지 마십시오. 그는 악한 자에게 속해서 자기 동생을 죽였습니다. 그런데 그가 무엇 때문에 동생을 죽였습니까?
ko.B: 여러분이 처음부터 들은 소식은 이것입니다. 우리는 서로 사랑해야 합니다. \v 12 가인처럼 되어서는 안 됩니다. 가인은 악한 자에게 속하여 자기 동생을 죽였습니다. 그가 왜 동생을 죽였습니까?
ko.R: 여러분은 맨 처음부터 이 소식을 들었습니다. 우리는 서로 사랑해야 합니다. \v 12 우리는 가인처럼 되어서는 안 됩니다. 가인은 악한 자, 곧 마귀에게 속했고, 자기 친동생을 죽였습니다. 그가 왜 동생을 죽였습니까?

decisions.choice: one record for 3:11 and the first part of 3:12
alternatives: two records, split at the raised dot after 3:11
decisions.reason: SBLGNT puts a raised dot after "love one another", but the words that follow, "not as Cain", cannot stand alone: they complete the command by setting Cain beside it as the opposite example. The record therefore runs on to the question at the end of the first part of 3:12.

decisions.choice: the message heard from the beginning: the teaching the readers received when they first heard the gospel
decisions.reason: ἀγγελία is the word used in 1:5. "From the beginning" here means from the start of the readers' life as believers, as in 2:7 and 2:24; Jesus gave the command to love one another to his disciples (John 13:34; 15:12).

decisions.choice: Cain, who killed his brother Abel
decisions.reason: Genesis 4:1-16 tells how Cain, angry that God accepted his brother's offering and not his, killed Abel. It is the Bible's first murder and the first hatred of a brother; the letter uses it as the pattern of what love is not.

decisions.choice: the evil one: the devil
decisions.reason: πονηροῦ with the article is a name for the devil in this letter (2:13-14; 5:18-19). To be "of" him is to belong to him, as in 3:8 and 3:10.

decisions.choice: slaughtered: killed violently, cut down
decisions.reason: σφάζω is used of slaughtering animals and of violent death (Revelation 5:6, 9; 6:9). It stresses the brutality of the act.

decisions.choice: murdered (Balanced); killed (Readable); slaughtered (Literal)
decisions.reason: In English "slaughtered" is mostly said of animals or of many people; "murdered" keeps the violence of a deliberate killing and prepares for "murderer" in 3:15. Literal keeps "slaughtered" so the force of the word stays visible.

decisions.choice: We must not be like Cain
decisions.reason: The Greek is a short phrase hanging on the command. Balanced and Readable give it a subject and verb so it reads as a sentence. Readable also names the evil one as the devil, following the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: a égorgé (L); a assassiné (B); a tué (R)
decisions.reason: "Égorger" keeps the violence of the Greek verb, which is used for cutting a throat (m5). Balanced says "assassiner" for a deliberate killing, as the English says "murdered". The past is in the passé composé at every level, as everywhere in the letter.

decisions.choice: degolló (L); asesinó (B); mató (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal keeps the violent verb (meaning decision m5) with "degollar", to cut a throat; Balanced and Readable use the common verbs.

decisions.choice: akamchinja (L); akamuua (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb is to kill violently, to cut down (m5). Literal keeps the force with "kuchinja" (slaughter); Balanced and Readable say "kuua" (kill), as the English says "murdered" and "killed". Cain is "Kaini", as in Hebrews 11:4 and Jude 11.

decisions.choice: "가인"; "동생" for Abel, Cain's brother; "죽이다" for slaughtered
decisions.reason: Cain killed his brother Abel (meaning decision). Korean names brothers by age, and Abel was the younger (Genesis 4:2), so "동생" is natural; a gender span would not fit one particular man. "죽이다" is the plain verb; the violence the meaning decision describes is clear from the story.

source.text: ὅτι τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ πονηρὰ ἦν, τὰ δὲ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ δίκαια.

records.literal_gloss: Because the works of him evil were, but those of the brother of him righteous.

en.L: Because his works were evil, but those of his brother [were] righteous.
en.B: Because his own deeds were evil, and his brother's were righteous.
en.R: Because the things Cain did were evil, and the things his brother Abel did were right.

fr.L: Parce que ses œuvres étaient mauvaises, et celles de son frère justes.
fr.B: Parce que ses propres actions étaient mauvaises, et que celles de son frère étaient justes.
fr.R: Parce que ce que faisait Caïn était mal, et que ce que faisait son frère Abel était bien.

es.L: Porque sus obras eran malas, pero las de su hermano [eran] justas.
es.B: Porque sus propias obras eran malas, y las de su hermano eran justas.
es.R: Porque lo que hacía Caín era malo, y lo que hacía su hermano Abel era justo.

sw.L: Kwa sababu matendo yake yalikuwa maovu, ila yale ya ndugu yake [yalikuwa] ya haki.
sw.B: Ni kwa sababu yeye mwenyewe alitenda maovu, na ndugu yake alitenda yaliyo ya haki.
sw.R: Kwa sababu mambo ambayo Kaini alifanya yalikuwa maovu, na mambo ambayo ndugu yake Habili alifanya yalikuwa ya haki.

ko.L: 그 자신의 행위는 악하였고, 그 동생의 [행위는] 의로웠기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 그 자신의 행위는 악했고, 그 동생의 행위는 의로웠기 때문입니다.
ko.R: 가인이 한 일은 악했고, 그의 동생 아벨이 한 일은 옳았기 때문입니다.

decisions.choice: Cain killed his brother because his own life was evil and his brother's was right
alternatives: Cain killed out of envy over the offering only
decisions.reason: The answer goes behind the story in Genesis 4:3-8 to its cause: evil hates what is right because it is shown up by it (John 3:19-20). Hebrews 11:4 also says Abel was counted righteous. This leads straight into 3:13: the world will hate the righteous in the same way.

decisions.choice: righteous: right in God's sight
decisions.reason: δίκαιος is the adjective used of Christ in 3:7; here it describes Abel's deeds as pleasing to God.

decisions.choice: Cain; his brother Abel
decisions.reason: Readable names Cain and Abel, since the answer comes after a question and the pronouns would be hard to follow. Abel is named in Genesis 4, the passage referred to.

source.text: μὴ θαυμάζετε, ἀδελφοί, εἰ μισεῖ ὑμᾶς ὁ κόσμος.

records.literal_gloss: Not be amazed, brothers, if hates you the world.

en.L: Do not be amazed, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, if the world hates you.
en.B: Do not be astonished, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, if the world hates you.
en.R: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, do not be shocked if the world hates you.

fr.L: Ne vous étonnez pas, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, si le monde vous hait.
fr.B: Ne soyez pas surpris, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, si le monde vous hait.
fr.R: {{gender:Frères et sœurs|Frères}}, ne soyez pas choqués si le monde vous déteste.

es.L: No {{plural_you:se maravillen|os maravilléis}}, hermanos, si el mundo {{plural_you:los|os}} odia.
es.B: No {{plural_you:se extrañen|os extrañéis}}, hermanos, si el mundo {{plural_you:los|os}} odia.
es.R: Hermanos, no {{plural_you:se sorprendan|os sorprendáis}} si el mundo {{plural_you:los|os}} odia.

sw.L: Msishangae, ndugu, ikiwa ulimwengu unawachukia.
sw.B: Ndugu zangu, msione ajabu ulimwengu ukiwachukia.
sw.R: Ndugu zangu, msishtuke ulimwengu ukiwachukia.

ko.L: {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 세상이 여러분을 미워해도 놀라지 마십시오.
ko.B: {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 세상이 여러분을 미워하더라도 이상하게 여기지 마십시오.
ko.R: {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 세상이 여러분을 미워하더라도 놀라지 마십시오.

decisions.choice: brothers: fellow believers, men and women
decisions.reason: The only place in the letter where the readers are called ἀδελφοί. The masculine plural is the ordinary way to address a group of men and women; the word picks up the brothers Cain and Abel.

decisions.choice: if: the condition is taken as real, close to "that"
decisions.reason: εἰ with the present tense here states something that is already the case for the readers, as in John 15:18.

decisions.choice: the world's hatred: echoes Jesus's warning to his disciples
decisions.reason: Jesus told his disciples, "If the world hates you, know that it hated me before you" (John 15:18-19; 17:14). Here the hatred also follows from the example of Cain (3:12).

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The gender setting gives the inclusive default and the traditional form, as the style guide asks.

decisions.choice: {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} for the readers (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As in English and in Colossians, the church is addressed as men and women together (m1); "frères" stays available as the traditional form. Words that agree with the noun need no span ("surpris", "choqués").

decisions.choice: hermanos, no setting
decisions.reason: As in Philippians and 1 John 5, the plural "hermanos" already covers brothers and sisters, so it takes no gender setting. The same in verses 14 and 16.

decisions.choice: ndugu (L); ndugu zangu (B, R); no gender span
alternatives: ndugu wa kiume na wa kike
decisions.reason: "Ndugu" already means brothers and sisters, fellow believers of either sex (m1), so the English span "brothers and sisters|brothers" has no Swahili counterpart, here or in verses 14 and 16.

source.text: ἡμεῖς οἴδαμεν ὅτι μεταβεβήκαμεν ἐκ τοῦ θανάτου εἰς τὴν ζωήν, ὅτι ἀγαπῶμεν τοὺς ἀδελφούς· ὁ μὴ ἀγαπῶν μένει ἐν τῷ θανάτῳ.

records.literal_gloss: We know that we have passed over out of the death into the life, because we love the brothers; the [one] not loving remains in the death.

en.L: We know that we have passed out of death into life, because we love the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}; the one who does not love remains in death.
en.B: We know that we have moved out of death into life, because we love our {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}. Whoever does not love remains in death.
en.R: We know that we have left death behind and come into life, because we love our {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}. Anyone who does not love remains in death.

fr.L: Nous savons que nous sommes passés de la mort dans la vie, parce que nous aimons les {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} ; celui qui n’aime pas demeure dans la mort.
fr.B: Nous savons que nous sommes passés de la mort à la vie, parce que nous aimons nos {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}. Celui qui n’aime pas demeure dans la mort.
fr.R: Nous savons que nous avons quitté la mort pour entrer dans la vie, parce que nous aimons nos {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}. Celui qui n’aime pas demeure dans la mort.

es.L: Nosotros sabemos que hemos pasado de la muerte a la vida, porque amamos a los hermanos; el que no ama permanece en la muerte.
es.B: Sabemos que hemos salido de la muerte y entrado en la vida, porque amamos a nuestros hermanos. Quien no ama permanece en la muerte.
es.R: Sabemos que hemos dejado atrás la muerte y hemos entrado en la vida, porque amamos a nuestros hermanos. Quien no ama sigue en la muerte.

sw.L: Sisi tunajua kwamba tumevuka kutoka katika mauti kuingia katika uzima, kwa sababu tunawapenda ndugu; yule asiyependa anakaa katika mauti.
sw.B: Tunajua kwamba tumetoka katika mauti tukaingia katika uzima, kwa sababu tunawapenda ndugu zetu. Yeyote asiyependa anakaa katika mauti.
sw.R: Tunajua kwamba tumeiacha mauti nyuma na kuingia katika uzima, kwa sababu tunawapenda ndugu zetu. Mtu yeyote asiyependa anakaa katika mauti.

ko.L: 우리는 우리가 죽음에서 생명으로 옮겨 갔다는 것을 압니다. 우리가 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}들을 사랑하기 때문입니다. 사랑하지 않는 사람은 죽음 가운데 머물러 있습니다.
ko.B: 우리는 우리가 죽음에서 생명으로 옮겨 갔다는 것을 압니다. 우리가 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}들을 사랑하기 때문입니다. 사랑하지 않는 사람은 죽음 가운데 머물러 있습니다.
ko.R: 우리는 우리가 죽음을 떠나 생명으로 들어왔다는 것을 압니다. 우리가 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}들을 사랑하기 때문입니다. 사랑하지 않는 사람은 여전히 죽음 가운데 머물러 있습니다.

decisions.choice: passed out of death into life: Jesus's own words
decisions.reason: John 5:24 uses the same verb and phrase of the one who hears Jesus's word and believes: such a person "has passed out of death into life". The perfect tense describes a move already made, with lasting effect.

decisions.choice: because we love: love is how we know, not what moved us into life
alternatives: we passed into life because we loved
decisions.reason: ὅτι goes with "we know": love for fellow believers is the evidence that the change has happened. The cause of the change is God's gift (3:1, 3:9; John 5:24).

decisions.choice: the brothers: fellow believers, men and women
decisions.reason: As in 3:10 and 3:13, the members of God's family.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "the one who does not love", without an object
alternatives: "the one who does not love his brother"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "his brother"; important early manuscripts have the shorter text, and the added words look like a natural filling out from 3:10. The meaning is the same. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: moved out of death into life (Balanced); left death behind and come into life (Readable)
decisions.reason: The same wording as Balanced and Readable at John 5:24, so the echo stays visible in English.

decisions.choice: passés de la mort dans la vie (L); de la mort à la vie (B); avons quitté la mort pour entrer dans la vie (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording as the French of John 5:24 at each level, so the echo of Jesus's words (m1) stays audible, as the English keeps it.

decisions.choice: mauti; uzima
decisions.reason: These are Jesus's own words (m1), death and life as two realms. "Mauti" is death as a state one can be in, as "uzima" is life; "kifo" (5:16) is the event of dying. "Uzima" is the word for life through the letter.

source.text: πᾶς ὁ μισῶν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ ἀνθρωποκτόνος ἐστίν, καὶ οἴδατε ὅτι πᾶς ἀνθρωποκτόνος οὐκ ἔχει ζωὴν αἰώνιον ἐν αὐτῷ μένουσαν.

records.literal_gloss: Everyone hating the brother of him a murderer is, and you know that every murderer not has life eternal in him remaining.

en.L: Everyone who hates {{gender:their brother or sister|his brother}} is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life remaining in {{gender:them|him}}.
en.B: Whoever hates {{gender:a brother or sister|a brother}} is a murderer, and you know that eternal life does not remain in any murderer.
en.R: Anyone who hates a fellow believer is a murderer at heart. And you know that no murderer has eternal life remaining in {{gender:them|him}}.

fr.L: Quiconque hait {{gender:son frère ou sa sœur|son frère}} est un meurtrier, et vous savez qu’aucun meurtrier n’a la vie éternelle demeurant en lui.
fr.B: Celui qui hait {{gender:un frère ou une sœur|un frère}} est un meurtrier, et vous savez que la vie éternelle ne demeure en aucun meurtrier.
fr.R: Celui qui hait un frère ou une sœur dans la foi est un meurtrier dans son cœur. Et vous savez qu’aucun meurtrier n’a la vie éternelle qui demeure en lui.

es.L: Todo el que odia a {{gender:su hermano o hermana|su hermano}} es un asesino, y {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} que ningún asesino tiene la vida eterna permaneciendo en su interior.
es.B: Quien odia a {{gender:un hermano o una hermana|un hermano}} es un asesino, y {{plural_you:ustedes saben|vosotros sabéis}} que la vida eterna no permanece en ningún asesino.
es.R: Quien odia a {{gender:un hermano o una hermana en la fe|un hermano en la fe}} es un asesino en su corazón. Y {{plural_you:ustedes saben|vosotros sabéis}} que ningún asesino tiene la vida eterna dentro de sí.

sw.L: Yeyote anayemchukia ndugu yake ni muuaji, na mnafahamu kwamba muuaji yeyote hana uzima wa milele unaokaa ndani yake.
sw.B: Yeyote anayemchukia ndugu yake ni muuaji, nanyi mnajua kwamba uzima wa milele haukai ndani ya muuaji yeyote.
sw.R: Mtu anayemchukia mwamini mwenzake ni muuaji moyoni mwake. Nanyi mnajua kwamba muuaji hawezi kuwa na uzima wa milele unaokaa ndani yake.

ko.L: 자기 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}를 미워하는 사람은 누구나 살인자입니다. 그리고 여러분이 알다시피, 살인자는 누구도 자기 안에 영원한 생명이 머물러 있지 않습니다.
ko.B: {{gender:형제자매|형제}}를 미워하는 사람은 살인자입니다. 그리고 여러분이 알다시피, 어떤 살인자에게도 영원한 생명이 머물러 있지 않습니다.
ko.R: 믿음의 식구를 미워하는 사람은 마음속으로 살인하는 사람입니다. 그리고 여러분이 알다시피, 살인하는 사람 안에는 영원한 생명이 머물러 있지 않습니다.

decisions.choice: to hate is to be a murderer in the heart
alternatives: hatred is as bad as murder in every respect
decisions.reason: Hatred is the root that Cain's murder grew from (3:12). Jesus taught the same: anger against a brother falls under the commandment against murder (Matthew 5:21-22). The point is the inner reality, not that the law should treat hatred as murder.

decisions.choice: murderer: one who kills a person
decisions.reason: ἀνθρωποκτόνος means a killer of people. In the New Testament it occurs only here and in John 8:44, where Jesus calls the devil "a murderer from the beginning"; the one who hates shares the devil's character (3:8, 3:10).

decisions.choice: eternal life and hatred cannot live together in a person
alternatives: a murderer can never be forgiven
decisions.reason: The verse describes the person whose life is ruled by hatred, as the present participle "hating" shows; it is not saying that someone who has killed can never be forgiven (1:9). Eternal life is a life that remains in a person, and hatred shows that it is not there.

decisions.choice: {{gender:their brother or sister|his brother}} (Literal); {{gender:a brother or sister|a brother}} (Balanced); a fellow believer (Readable)
decisions.reason: The gender setting gives the inclusive default and the traditional form. Readable says "a fellow believer", as at 3:10.

decisions.choice: a murderer at heart
decisions.reason: Readable adds "at heart" so a young reader does not take the verse to say that hating someone is the same crime as killing them; it follows the meaning decision on hatred and murder.

source.text: ἐν τούτῳ ἐγνώκαμεν τὴν ἀγάπην, ὅτι ἐκεῖνος ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἔθηκεν· καὶ ἡμεῖς ὀφείλομεν ὑπὲρ τῶν ἀδελφῶν τὰς ψυχὰς θεῖναι.

records.literal_gloss: By this we have known the love: that that one for us the life of him laid down; and we ought for the brothers the lives to lay down.

en.L: By this we have come to know love: that that one laid down {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} life for us; and we ought to lay down [our] lives for the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}.
en.B: This is how we have come to know what love is: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} laid down {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} life for us. And we in turn owe it to our {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} to lay down our lives for them.
en.R: This is how we know what love is: Jesus gave up {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} life for us. So we also must give up our lives for our {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}.

fr.L: À ceci nous avons connu l’amour : celui-là a déposé {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} vie pour nous ; et nous, nous devons déposer [nos] vies pour les {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}.
fr.B: Voici comment nous avons appris ce qu’est l’amour : {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a donné {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} vie pour nous. Et nous, à notre tour, nous devons à nos {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} de donner notre vie pour eux.
fr.R: Voici comment nous savons ce qu’est l’amour : Jésus a donné {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} vie pour nous. Alors nous aussi, nous devons donner notre vie pour nos {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}.

es.L: En esto hemos conocido el amor: en que aquel puso {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} vida por nosotros; y nosotros debemos poner [nuestras] vidas por los hermanos.
es.B: Así hemos llegado a conocer lo que es el amor: {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} entregó {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} vida por nosotros. Y nosotros, a nuestra vez, les debemos a nuestros hermanos entregar nuestra vida por ellos.
es.R: Así sabemos lo que es el amor: Jesús dio {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} vida por nosotros. Por eso nosotros también debemos dar nuestra vida por nuestros hermanos.

sw.L: Kwa hili tumeujua upendo: kwamba yule aliyatoa maisha {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kwa ajili yetu; nasi tunapaswa kuyatoa maisha [yetu] kwa ajili ya ndugu.
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo tulivyokuja kujua upendo ni nini: {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} aliyatoa maisha {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kwa ajili yetu. Nasi pia tuna deni kwa ndugu zetu la kuyatoa maisha yetu kwa ajili yao.
sw.R: Hivi ndivyo tunavyojua upendo ni nini: Yesu aliyatoa maisha {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kwa ajili yetu. Kwa hiyo nasi pia lazima tuyatoe maisha yetu kwa ajili ya ndugu zetu.

ko.L: 이것으로 우리는 사랑을 알게 되었습니다. 그분이 우리를 위하여 자기 목숨을 내놓으셨다는 것입니다. 그러므로 우리도 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}들을 위하여 [우리의] 목숨을 내놓아야 합니다.
ko.B: 그분이 우리를 위해 자기 목숨을 내놓으셨습니다. 이것으로 우리는 사랑이 무엇인지 알게 되었습니다. 그러므로 우리도 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}들을 위해 우리 목숨을 내놓아야 마땅합니다.
ko.R: 사랑이 무엇인지 우리는 이렇게 압니다. 예수님께서 우리를 위해 자기 목숨을 내주셨습니다. 그러니 우리도 우리 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}들을 위해 우리 목숨을 내주어야 합니다.

decisions.choice: lay down one's life: give one's life up willingly, die for others
decisions.reason: The phrase is Jesus's own in John 10:11-18 ("the good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep") and 15:13. It speaks of a death freely chosen for the sake of others.

decisions.choice: by this ... that: love is defined by what Christ did
decisions.reason: ὅτι spells out the "this": we know what love is by looking at the cross. "That one" is Christ, as in 3:3, 3:5 and 3:7.

decisions.choice: ought: a debt that follows from what Christ did
decisions.reason: ὀφείλω is the language of owing (2:6; 4:11). Because Christ gave his life for us, we owe the same love to one another. Verse 17 shows the everyday form of it: sharing what we have.

decisions.choice: the brothers: fellow believers, men and women
decisions.reason: As in 3:14.

decisions.choice: owe it to (Balanced); must (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the sense of debt in the verb; Readable says it as a plain obligation. Readable also says "gave up his life", as at John 10:11, and names Jesus for "that one".

decisions.choice: a déposé sa vie (L); a donné sa vie (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in the French of John 10:11: Literal keeps the image of laying down, and Balanced and Readable say "donner sa vie", the French idiom for dying for others (m1).

decisions.choice: kuyatoa maisha
decisions.reason: To lay down one's life is to give it up willingly and die for others (m1). "Maisha" is the word the project uses for this Greek word for life, as in the Gospels; "uzima" is kept for the life of God, and "nafsi" would suggest the soul.

decisions.choice: "목숨" for life laid down; "내놓다" (L, B), "내주다" (R)
decisions.reason: The Korean style guide keeps "목숨" for this word (psychē) and "생명" for the life God gives (zōē); to lay down one's life is to die for others (meaning decision), as in the Korean John 10:11 and 15:13.

source.text: ὃς δ’ ἂν ἔχῃ τὸν βίον τοῦ κόσμου καὶ θεωρῇ τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ χρείαν ἔχοντα καὶ κλείσῃ τὰ σπλάγχνα αὐτοῦ ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ, πῶς ἡ ἀγάπη τοῦ θεοῦ μένει ἐν αὐτῷ;

records.literal_gloss: But whoever has the livelihood of the world and sees the brother of him need having and shuts the inner parts of him from him, how the love of the God remains in him?

en.L: But whoever has the world's goods and sees {{gender:their brother or sister|his brother}} having need, and shuts {{gender:their|his}} heart against {{gender:them|him}}, how does the love of God remain in {{gender:that person|him}}?
en.B: Suppose someone has enough of this world's goods and notices {{gender:a brother or sister|a brother}} in need, yet shuts {{gender:their|his}} heart against {{gender:them|him}}. How can the love of God remain in such a person?
en.R: Suppose someone has money and possessions in this world, and sees a fellow believer in need, but refuses to show {{gender:them|him}} any pity. How can God's love remain in that person?

fr.L: Mais celui qui a les biens du monde, et qui voit {{gender:son frère ou sa sœur|son frère}} dans le besoin, et lui ferme son cœur, comment l’amour de Dieu demeure-t-il en lui ?
fr.B: Supposons que quelqu’un ait assez des biens de ce monde et voie {{gender:un frère ou une sœur|un frère}} dans le besoin, mais lui ferme son cœur. Comment l’amour de Dieu pourrait-il demeurer en lui ?
fr.R: Imaginons quelqu’un qui a de l’argent et des biens dans ce monde. Il voit un frère ou une sœur dans la foi qui est dans le besoin, mais il refuse d’en avoir pitié. Comment l’amour de Dieu peut-il demeurer en lui ?

es.L: Pero el que tiene los bienes del mundo y ve a {{gender:su hermano o hermana|su hermano}} pasar necesidad, y le cierra sus entrañas, ¿cómo permanece el amor de Dios en {{gender:esa persona|él}}?
