es.B: Supongamos que alguien tiene bienes de este mundo y ve a {{gender:un hermano o una hermana|un hermano}} en necesidad, pero le cierra su corazón. ¿Cómo puede permanecer el amor de Dios en una persona así?
es.R: Supongamos que alguien tiene dinero y cosas en este mundo, y ve a {{gender:un hermano o una hermana en la fe|un hermano en la fe}} en necesidad, pero no quiere tener compasión. ¿Cómo puede permanecer el amor de Dios en esa persona?

sw.L: Lakini mtu yeyote mwenye riziki ya ulimwengu, akamwona ndugu yake ana mahitaji, akamfungia moyo wake, upendo wa Mungu unakaaje ndani yake?
sw.B: Tuseme mtu ana mali ya kutosha ya ulimwengu huu, akamwona ndugu yake mwenye shida, lakini akamfungia moyo wake. Upendo wa Mungu unawezaje kukaa ndani ya mtu wa namna hiyo?
sw.R: Tuseme mtu ana fedha na mali katika ulimwengu huu, akamwona mwamini mwenzake mwenye shida, lakini akakataa kumhurumia. Upendo wa Mungu unawezaje kukaa ndani ya mtu huyo?

ko.L: 그러나 누구든지 세상의 재물을 가지고 있으면서 자기 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}가 궁핍한 것을 보고도 그에게 마음을 닫는다면, 하나님의 사랑이 어떻게 그 사람 안에 머물겠습니까?
ko.B: 어떤 사람이 이 세상의 재물을 넉넉히 가지고 있으면서도 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}가 어려움에 처한 것을 보고 마음을 닫는다고 합시다. 하나님의 사랑이 어떻게 그런 사람 안에 머물러 있을 수 있겠습니까?
ko.R: 어떤 사람이 이 세상에서 돈과 재산을 가지고 있으면서, 믿음의 식구가 어려움에 처한 것을 보고도 조금도 불쌍히 여기지 않는다고 해 봅시다. 하나님의 사랑이 어떻게 그런 사람 안에 머물러 있을 수 있겠습니까?

decisions.choice: the world's goods: the means of living, money and possessions
decisions.reason: βίος is life in the sense of livelihood, what one lives on (Mark 12:44; Luke 15:12), as in 2:16. It is set beside verse 16: if we owe our lives to one another, we surely owe our goods.

decisions.choice: shut one's heart: refuse compassion
decisions.reason: σπλάγχνα are the inner organs, which Greek speakers thought of as the seat of feelings of pity, much as "heart" is used today. To shut them against someone is to refuse to feel for them or help them.

decisions.choice: the love of God: God's love, at home in a person
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean either the love God has or the love we have for God. In this letter it is the love that comes from God and is made complete in those who obey him (2:5; 4:9-12). Someone who shuts out a needy brother or sister shows that this love is not living in them. The two readings overlap, since the love that comes from God is also love returned to him (4:20).

decisions.choice: how ...?: a question that expects the answer "it cannot"
decisions.reason: The question is a strong denial: God's love cannot remain in such a person.

decisions.choice: heart
decisions.reason: Even Literal says "heart": a word for word "inward parts" would hide the meaning in English, as the idiom decision explains.

decisions.choice: money and possessions; a fellow believer; refuses to show them any pity
alternatives: the world's goods; his brother; shuts his heart
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idioms mean, following the meaning decisions, and uses "a fellow believer" as at 3:10 and 3:15.

decisions.choice: entrañas (L); corazón (B)
decisions.reason: As in Philippians 1:8: Literal keeps "entrañas", the inner organs as the seat of pity, and Balanced says "corazón". "Le cierra" does not mark gender, so the English span "them|him" needs no counterpart.

decisions.choice: riziki ya ulimwengu (L); mali ya ulimwengu huu (B); fedha na mali (R)
decisions.reason: The word, the same as "life" in 2:16, here means the means of living, money and possessions (m1). Literal says "riziki" (livelihood) and Balanced "mali" (goods, wealth); "maisha" would not be understood as property.

decisions.choice: moyo
decisions.reason: The Greek word is the inward parts, the seat of compassion (m2). Swahili "moyo" (heart) is the seat of compassion, as the project's term list sets for this word.

source.text: Τεκνία, μὴ ἀγαπῶμεν λόγῳ μηδὲ τῇ γλώσσῃ ἀλλὰ ἐν ἔργῳ καὶ ἀληθείᾳ.

records.literal_gloss: Little children, not let us love in word nor in the tongue, but in deed and truth.

en.L: Little children, let us not love with word nor with the tongue, but in deed and truth.
en.B: Dear children, let us love not by what we say or with our tongues, but by what we do and in truth.
en.R: Dear children, let us not just say that we love others. Let us really love them by what we do, and in truth.

fr.L: Petits enfants, n’aimons pas en parole ni avec la langue, mais en acte et en vérité.
fr.B: Mes chers enfants, aimons, non par nos paroles ou avec notre langue, mais par nos actes et en vérité.
fr.R: Mes chers enfants, ne nous contentons pas de dire que nous aimons les autres. Aimons-les vraiment, par ce que nous faisons, et en vérité.

es.L: Hijitos, no amemos de palabra ni de lengua, sino de hecho y en verdad.
es.B: Hijitos, no amemos solo con lo que decimos ni con la lengua, sino con lo que hacemos y en verdad.
es.R: Hijos queridos, no digamos solamente que amamos a los demás. Amémoslos de verdad con lo que hacemos y en verdad.

sw.L: Watoto wadogo, tusiwe tukipenda kwa neno wala kwa ulimi, bali katika tendo na katika kweli.
sw.B: Wanangu wapendwa, tusipende kwa yale tunayosema au kwa ndimi zetu tu, bali kwa yale tunayotenda na katika kweli.
sw.R: Wanangu wapendwa, tusiseme tu kwamba tunawapenda wengine. Tuwapende kweli kwa matendo yetu, na katika kweli.

ko.L: 어린 자녀 여러분, 우리는 말로나 혀로 사랑하지 말고, 행함과 진리로 사랑합시다.
ko.B: 어린 자녀 여러분, 우리는 말이나 혀로만 사랑하지 말고, 행동과 진실함으로 사랑합시다.
ko.R: 사랑하는 자녀 여러분, 우리는 다른 사람을 사랑한다고 말만 하지 맙시다. 우리가 하는 일로, 그리고 진실하게 그들을 정말로 사랑합시다.

decisions.choice: not by words alone but in deeds: love that stays in talk is not love
alternatives: words of love are wrong in themselves
decisions.reason: The contrast is sharp, but the point is that love must not stop at words, as the needy brother or sister of 3:17 shows (James 2:15-16). Kind words are not forbidden; empty ones are.

decisions.choice: truth: genuine, real, and in keeping with God's truth
decisions.reason: ἀλήθεια here means love that is real rather than pretended, but in this letter truth is also what comes from God (3:19, "of the truth"; 1:6, 2:4). Love in deed and truth is love that matches what God is.

decisions.choice: Little children (Literal); Dear children (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As at 3:7.

decisions.choice: others; them
decisions.reason: Readable supplies who is to be loved, the fellow believers of 3:16-17, and "really" for the contrast with mere talk.

decisions.choice: "진리로" (L); "진실함으로" (B); "진실하게" (R)
decisions.reason: Truth here is love that is genuine, real and in keeping with God's truth (meaning decision). Literal keeps the key term; Balanced and Readable say "genuinely", since "진리로 사랑하다" reads as loving by means of doctrine.

source.text: ἐν τούτῳ γνωσόμεθα ὅτι ἐκ τῆς ἀληθείας ἐσμέν, καὶ ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ πείσομεν τὴν καρδίαν ἡμῶν ὅτι ἐὰν καταγινώσκῃ ἡμῶν ἡ καρδία, ὅτι μείζων ἐστὶν ὁ θεὸς τῆς καρδίας ἡμῶν καὶ γινώσκει πάντα.

records.literal_gloss: By this we will know that of the truth we are, and before him we will persuade the heart of us, \v 20 that if condemns us the heart, that greater is the God than the heart of us and he knows all things.

en.L: By this we will know that we are of the truth, and before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} we will persuade our heart \v 20 that if our heart condemns [us], that God is greater than our heart and knows all things.
en.B: This is how we will know that we belong to the truth, and how we will set our hearts at rest in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence \v 20 whenever our hearts condemn us: God is greater than our hearts, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} knows everything.
en.R: That is how we will know that we belong to the truth. And when we stand before God, we can calm our hearts \v 20 even when they accuse us. For God is greater than our hearts, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} knows everything.

fr.L: À ceci nous saurons que nous sommes de la vérité, et devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} nous persuaderons notre cœur, \v 20 que, si notre cœur nous condamne, Dieu est plus grand que notre cœur et connaît toutes choses.
fr.B: C’est ainsi que nous saurons que nous appartenons à la vérité, et que nous apaiserons notre cœur devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} \v 20 chaque fois que notre cœur nous condamnera : Dieu est plus grand que notre cœur, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} connaît tout.
fr.R: Voilà comment nous saurons que nous appartenons à la vérité. Et quand nous serons devant Dieu, nous pourrons calmer notre cœur, \v 20 même quand il nous accuse. Car Dieu est plus grand que notre cœur, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sait tout.

es.L: En esto sabremos que somos de la verdad, y delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} persuadiremos a nuestro corazón \v 20 de que, si nuestro corazón [nos] condena, Dios es mayor que nuestro corazón y conoce todas las cosas.
es.B: Así sabremos que pertenecemos a la verdad, y así tranquilizaremos nuestro corazón en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} presencia \v 20 cada vez que nuestro corazón nos condene: Dios es mayor que nuestro corazón, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} lo sabe todo.
es.R: Así sabremos que pertenecemos a la verdad. Y cuando estemos delante de Dios, podremos calmar nuestro corazón \v 20 aun cuando nos acuse. Porque Dios es mayor que nuestro corazón, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} lo sabe todo.

sw.L: Kwa hili tutatambua kwamba tunatoka katika kweli, na mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} tutautuliza moyo wetu \v 20 kwamba, ikiwa moyo wetu unatuhukumu, Mungu ni mkubwa kuliko moyo wetu, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} anajua mambo yote.
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo tutakavyojua kwamba tunatoka katika kweli, na jinsi tutakavyoituliza mioyo yetu mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} \v 20 kila mioyo yetu inapotuhukumu: Mungu ni mkuu zaidi ya mioyo yetu, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} anajua kila kitu.
sw.R: Hivyo ndivyo tutakavyojua kwamba sisi ni wa kweli. Na tunaposimama mbele ya Mungu, tunaweza kuituliza mioyo yetu \v 20 hata inapotushtaki. Kwa maana Mungu ni mkuu kuliko mioyo yetu, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} anajua kila kitu.

ko.L: 이것으로 우리는 우리가 진리에 속해 있다는 것을 알게 될 것이고, 그분 앞에서 우리 마음을 설득할 것입니다. \v 20 우리 마음이 우리를 정죄하더라도, 하나님은 우리 마음보다 크시고 모든 것을 아신다는 것입니다.
ko.B: 이렇게 하여 우리는 우리가 진리에 속해 있다는 것을 알게 될 것이고, 그분 앞에서 우리 마음을 안심시킬 것입니다. \v 20 우리 마음이 우리를 정죄할 때마다 그렇게 할 것입니다. 하나님은 우리 마음보다 크시고, 모든 것을 아시기 때문입니다.
ko.R: 그렇게 하여 우리는 우리가 진리에 속해 있다는 것을 알게 될 것입니다. 그리고 하나님 앞에 설 때 우리 마음을 진정시킬 수 있습니다. \v 20 우리 마음이 우리를 고발할 때에도 그렇습니다. 하나님은 우리 마음보다 크시고, 모든 것을 아시기 때문입니다.

decisions.choice: by this: points back to loving in deed and truth (3:18)
decisions.reason: Love shown in action is how we will know that we belong to the truth. The future tense looks to the times when that assurance is needed.

decisions.choice: persuade: reassure, set at rest
decisions.reason: πείθω means to persuade; with the heart as its object it means to quiet it, as in Matthew 28:14, where the guards are told the governor will be "persuaded" and they kept out of trouble.

decisions.choice: we will reassure our hearts whenever they condemn us, because God is greater than our hearts
alternatives: "that if our heart condemns us, [we know] that God is greater": both words mean "that", the second repeating the first after the long condition
"because if our heart condemns us, God is greater": a warning, God judging even more strictly than our conscience
decisions.reason: The verse has two clauses introduced by ὅτι. The first, with the following ἐὰν, can be read as "whatever" or "whenever" (the same letters can be divided into two words meaning "whatever"), with the second ὅτι giving the reason: "because God is greater". Or both can mean "that", the second picking up the first after the long condition. All readings make God greater than the heart; they differ on whether that is a comfort or a warning. The grammar is difficult and no reading is free of strain.

decisions.choice: God's greatness is a comfort: he knows everything, including the love and the truth our accusing conscience overlooks
alternatives: a warning: if even our own heart condemns us, God, who knows everything, will condemn us more
decisions.reason: The passage is building assurance: "we will know", "we will set our hearts at rest", and 3:21 goes on, "if our heart does not condemn us, we have confidence". Peter's words in John 21:17, "Lord, you know everything; you know that I love you", show the same thought. Taken as a warning, the verse would cut against that flow, though it fits the seriousness of 3:15-17.

decisions.choice: heart: the conscience, our inner judgment of ourselves
decisions.reason: The heart here is the inner self that judges and condemns; καταγινώσκω means to condemn or find fault with.

decisions.choice: set our hearts at rest (Balanced); calm our hearts (Readable)
decisions.reason: Following the meaning decision on the verb. Balanced and Readable say "hearts" for the singular, since English speaks of each person's heart.

decisions.choice: when we stand before God; accuse
decisions.reason: Readable names God and says "accuse" for the heart's verdict, an everyday word for what conscience does.

decisions.choice: notre cœur, singular, at every level
decisions.reason: The English Balanced and Readable say "hearts" for the Greek singular. French speaks naturally of "notre cœur" for the conscience of each of us (m5), so every level keeps the singular, here and in 3:21.

decisions.choice: tranquilizar (B); calmar (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to reassure, set at rest (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps "persuadir"; Balanced and Readable say what it does to the heart.

decisions.choice: tutautuliza moyo wetu (L); tutakavyoituliza mioyo yetu (B); kuituliza mioyo yetu (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is to persuade in the sense of reassure, set at rest (m2). "Kutuliza" (calm, set at rest) says what the persuading does; "kushawishi" would suggest talking the heart into something. The heart is the conscience (m5); Literal keeps the Greek singular "moyo".

decisions.choice: "설득할 것입니다 ... 모든 것을 아신다는 것입니다" (L); "안심시킬 것입니다 ... 크시고 ... 아시기 때문입니다" (B, R)
alternatives: "우리 마음이 우리를 정죄하면 하나님은 더 크시니" as a threat
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the sentence as comfort: we will set our hearts at rest whenever they condemn us, because God is greater and knows everything, and footnotes other readings. Literal keeps the Greek's "that ... that" as one thing we persuade our hearts of; Balanced and Readable give the reason with "때문입니다".

source.text: ἀγαπητοί, ἐὰν ἡ καρδία μὴ καταγινώσκῃ ἡμῶν, παρρησίαν ἔχομεν πρὸς τὸν θεόν, καὶ ὃ ἐὰν αἰτῶμεν λαμβάνομεν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ, ὅτι τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ τηροῦμεν καὶ τὰ ἀρεστὰ ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ ποιοῦμεν.

records.literal_gloss: Beloved, if the heart not condemns us, confidence we have toward the God, \v 22 and whatever we ask we receive from him, because the commandments of him we keep and the things pleasing before him we do.

en.L: Beloved, if [our] heart does not condemn us, we have confidence toward God, \v 22 and whatever we ask we receive from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, because we keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands and do the things [that are] pleasing before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Dear friends, if our hearts do not condemn us, we can approach God boldly, \v 22 and whatever we ask, we receive from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, since we are keeping {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands and doing what is pleasing in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sight.
en.R: Dear friends, if our hearts do not accuse us, we can come to God without fear. \v 22 We receive from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} whatever we ask, because we obey {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands and do what pleases {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

fr.L: Bien-aimés, si le cœur ne nous condamne pas, nous avons de l’assurance devant Dieu, \v 22 et quoi que nous demandions, nous le recevons de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, parce que nous gardons {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} commandements et que nous faisons ce qui est agréable devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Chers amis, si notre cœur ne nous condamne pas, nous pouvons nous approcher de Dieu avec assurance, \v 22 et tout ce que nous demandons, nous le recevons de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, parce que nous gardons {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} commandements et que nous faisons ce qui est agréable à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} yeux.
fr.R: Chers amis, si notre cœur ne nous accuse pas, nous pouvons venir vers Dieu sans peur. \v 22 Nous recevons de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} tout ce que nous demandons, parce que nous obéissons à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} commandements et que nous faisons ce qui {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} plaît.

es.L: Amados, si [nuestro] corazón no nos condena, tenemos libertad ante Dios, \v 22 y cualquier cosa que pidamos la recibimos de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, porque guardamos {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} mandamientos y hacemos lo que es agradable delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Queridos amigos, si nuestro corazón no nos condena, podemos acercarnos a Dios con confianza, \v 22 y recibimos de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} todo lo que pedimos, porque guardamos {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} mandamientos y hacemos lo que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} agrada.
es.R: Queridos amigos, si nuestro corazón no nos acusa, podemos acercarnos a Dios sin miedo. \v 22 Recibimos de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} todo lo que pedimos, porque obedecemos {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} mandatos y hacemos lo que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} agrada.

sw.L: Wapendwa, ikiwa moyo [wetu] hautuhukumu, tuna uhuru tunapomwelekea Mungu, \v 22 na chochote tunachoomba tunakipokea kutoka {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, kwa sababu tunashika amri {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} na kufanya mambo yanayopendeza machoni {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}}.
sw.B: Rafiki zangu wapendwa, ikiwa mioyo yetu haituhukumu, tunaweza kumkaribia Mungu kwa ujasiri, \v 22 na chochote tunachoomba tunakipokea kutoka {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, kwa kuwa tunazishika amri {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} na kutenda yale yanayompendeza.
sw.R: Rafiki zangu wapendwa, ikiwa mioyo yetu haitushtaki, tunaweza kumwendea Mungu bila hofu. \v 22 Tunapokea kutoka {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} chochote tunachoomba, kwa sababu tunatii amri {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} na kufanya yale yanayompendeza.

ko.L: 사랑하는 여러분, 우리 마음이 우리를 정죄하지 않으면, 우리는 하나님 앞에서 담대함을 가집니다. \v 22 그리고 우리가 무엇을 구하든지 그분에게서 받습니다. 우리가 그분의 계명들을 지키고, 그분 앞에서 기뻐하시는 일들을 행하기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 사랑하는 여러분, 우리 마음이 우리를 정죄하지 않으면, 우리는 담대하게 하나님께 나아갈 수 있습니다. \v 22 그리고 무엇을 구하든지 그분에게서 받습니다. 우리가 그분의 계명을 지키고, 그분이 보시기에 기뻐하시는 일을 하고 있기 때문입니다.
ko.R: 사랑하는 여러분, 우리 마음이 우리를 고발하지 않으면, 우리는 두려움 없이 하나님께 나아갈 수 있습니다. \v 22 우리는 무엇이든지 구하는 대로 그분에게서 받습니다. 우리가 그분의 계명에 순종하고, 그분을 기쁘시게 하는 일을 하기 때문입니다.

decisions.choice: confidence: boldness, freedom to speak openly to God
decisions.reason: παρρησία is the freedom to speak openly, without fear (John 7:13, 26). In this letter it is the confidence of God's children before him, at Christ's coming (2:28; 4:17) and in prayer (5:14).

decisions.choice: obedience is the setting of answered prayer, not the price paid for it
alternatives: God grants requests as a reward for obedience
decisions.reason: Those who keep his commands live close to him and ask in line with his will (5:14-15; John 15:7, 15:10; 9:31). The present tenses describe the ongoing life of a child with a father, not a bargain.

decisions.choice: commands: what God has told his people to do
decisions.reason: ἐντολή is defined in the next verse: believing in his Son and loving one another (3:23).

decisions.choice: approach God boldly (Balanced); come to God without fear (Readable)
decisions.reason: Following the meaning decision on the word: the confidence is the freedom to come to God and speak openly.

decisions.choice: commands
decisions.reason: "Command" is the word used for the same noun in John 10:18; "commandments" now suggests mainly the Ten Commandments.

decisions.choice: libertad (L); confianza (B); sin miedo (R)
decisions.reason: As in 1 John 5:14, where the same word speaks of coming to God in prayer (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: uhuru (L); kwa ujasiri (B); bila hofu (R)
decisions.reason: As in 2:28 and 5:14: freedom to speak openly to God (m1). Literal says "uhuru", Balanced "ujasiri" (boldness), and Readable "bila hofu" (without fear), as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ ἐντολὴ αὐτοῦ, ἵνα πιστεύσωμεν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ἀγαπῶμεν ἀλλήλους, καθὼς ἔδωκεν ἐντολὴν ἡμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: And this is the commandment of him, that we believe the name of the Son of him Jesus Christ and we love one another, just as he gave commandment to us.

en.L: And this is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} command: that we believe the name of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} and love one another, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave [the] command to us.
en.B: This is what God commands: that we believe in the name of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, and that we love one another, following the command {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave us.
en.R: And this is what God commands us to do: believe in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, and love one another, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commanded us.

fr.L: Et voici {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} commandement : que nous croyions au nom de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}} et que nous nous aimions les uns les autres, comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous en a donné le commandement.
fr.B: Voici ce que Dieu commande : que nous croyions au nom de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}, et que nous nous aimions les uns les autres, selon le commandement qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous a donné.
fr.R: Et voici ce que Dieu nous commande : croire en {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}, et nous aimer les uns les autres, comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous l’a commandé.

es.L: Y este es {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mandamiento: que creamos en el nombre de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} y nos amemos unos a otros, tal como nos dio [el] mandamiento.
es.B: Esto es lo que Dios manda: que creamos en el nombre de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} y que nos amemos unos a otros, conforme al mandamiento que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} nos dio.
es.R: Y esto es lo que Dios nos manda hacer: creer en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} y amarnos unos a otros, como {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} nos mandó.

sw.L: Na amri {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ni hii: tuliamini jina la Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, na tupendane, sawasawa na amri {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} aliyotupa.
sw.B: Hiki ndicho Mungu anachoamuru: kwamba tuliamini jina la Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, na kwamba tupendane, kwa kufuata amri aliyotupa.
sw.R: Na hiki ndicho Mungu anachotuamuru tufanye: tumwamini Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, na tupendane, kama {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alivyotuamuru.

ko.L: 그리고 그분의 계명은 이것입니다. 우리가 그분의 아들 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 이름을 믿고, 그분이 우리에게 계명을 주신 대로 서로 사랑하는 것입니다.
ko.B: 하나님께서 명령하시는 것은 이것입니다. 우리가 그분의 아들 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 이름을 믿고, 그분이 우리에게 주신 계명대로 서로 사랑하는 것입니다.
ko.R: 하나님께서 우리에게 명령하시는 것은 이것입니다. 그분의 아들 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 믿고, 그분이 명령하신 대로 서로 사랑하십시오.

decisions.choice: believe the name: accept what his name says he is, and trust him
decisions.reason: The verb takes the name in the dative without a preposition, "believe the name", rather than "believe into the name" (John 1:12; 3:18). The name stands for the person as he is made known: Jesus, the Son of God, the Christ (5:1, 5:5). The two forms of words mean much the same.

decisions.choice: one command with two parts: believing and loving
decisions.reason: ἐντολὴ is singular, yet it holds both believing and loving. Faith in the Son and love for one another belong together as one thing God asks.

decisions.choice: he gave us the command: God, the "he" of the sentence
alternatives: Christ, who gave the command to love one another (John 13:34; 15:12)
decisions.reason: The sentence speaks of God's command and his Son, so the natural subject is God. But the command to love one another was given by Jesus in John 13:34, and 1 John often lets the words for God and Christ run together.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "believe" in the tense of a decisive act
alternatives: "believe" in the present tense, of continuing belief
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts have the present tense of the verb; SBLGNT prints the aorist, which also has strong early support. The meaning is hardly affected. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (Literal); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The christos setting, as in every passage.

decisions.choice: God (Balanced, Readable); believe in his Son (Readable)
alternatives: his command; believe in the name of his Son
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God for "his", since a new paragraph of thought begins here. Readable says "believe in his Son" because "the name" stands for the person, as the meaning decision says.

decisions.choice: croire au nom (L, B)
decisions.reason: The English Literal can say "believe the name"; French cannot put "le nom" as the object of "croire" in this sense, so Literal says "croire au nom", as Balanced does. Readable says "croire en son Fils", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: tuliamini jina (L, B); tumwamini Mwana (R)
decisions.reason: To believe the name is to accept what the name says he is and trust him (m1). "Kuliamini jina" keeps the Greek wording at Literal and Balanced; Readable says "believe in his Son", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "이름을 믿다" (L, B); "믿다" (R) for believe
decisions.reason: To believe the name is to accept what his name says he is, and trust him (meaning decision). "믿다" is the key-term verb at every level, as in the Korean John; Readable leaves out "name", as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ ὁ τηρῶν τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ μένει καὶ αὐτὸς ἐν αὐτῷ· καὶ ἐν τούτῳ γινώσκομεν ὅτι μένει ἐν ἡμῖν, ἐκ τοῦ πνεύματος οὗ ἡμῖν ἔδωκεν.

records.literal_gloss: And the [one] keeping the commandments of him in him remains and he in him; and by this we know that he remains in us, from the Spirit whom to us he gave.

en.L: And the one who keeps {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands remains in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} in {{gender:them|him}}; and by this we know that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} remains in us: from the Spirit whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave us.
en.B: Those who keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands remain in God, and God remains in them. We can be sure that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} remains in us because of the Spirit {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given us.
en.R: Those who obey God's commands remain in God, and God remains in them. The Spirit God has given us is how we know that God remains in us.

fr.L: Et celui qui garde {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} commandements demeure en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} en lui ; et à ceci nous savons qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} demeure en nous : par l’Esprit qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous a donné.
fr.B: Ceux qui gardent {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} commandements demeurent en Dieu, et Dieu demeure en eux. Nous pouvons être sûrs qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} demeure en nous grâce à l’Esprit qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous a donné.
fr.R: Ceux qui obéissent aux commandements de Dieu demeurent en Dieu, et Dieu demeure en eux. C’est grâce à l’Esprit que Dieu nous a donné que nous savons qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} demeure en nous.

es.L: Y el que guarda {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} mandamientos permanece en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} en {{gender:esa persona|él}}; y en esto sabemos que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} permanece en nosotros: por el Espíritu que nos dio.
es.B: Los que guardan {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} mandamientos permanecen en Dios, y Dios permanece en ellos. Podemos estar seguros de que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} permanece en nosotros por el Espíritu que nos ha dado.
es.R: Los que obedecen los mandatos de Dios permanecen en Dios, y Dios permanece en ellos. El Espíritu que Dios nos ha dado es la manera en que sabemos que Dios permanece en nosotros.

sw.L: Na anayeshika amri {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} anakaa ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ndani ya mtu huyo; na kwa hili tunajua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anakaa ndani yetu: kutokana na Roho ambaye ametupa.
sw.B: Wale wanaozishika amri {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} wanakaa ndani ya Mungu, na Mungu anakaa ndani yao. Tunaweza kuwa na hakika kwamba {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anakaa ndani yetu kwa sababu ya Roho ambaye ametupa.
sw.R: Wale wanaotii amri za Mungu wanakaa ndani ya Mungu, na Mungu anakaa ndani yao. Roho ambaye Mungu ametupa ndiye anayetuonyesha kwamba Mungu anakaa ndani yetu.

ko.L: 그리고 그분의 계명들을 지키는 사람은 그분 안에 머물고, 그분도 그 사람 안에 [머무십니다]. 그리고 그분이 우리 안에 머무신다는 것을 우리는 이것으로, 곧 그분이 우리에게 주신 성령으로 압니다.
ko.B: 하나님의 계명을 지키는 사람은 하나님 안에 머물러 있고, 하나님께서도 그 사람 안에 머물러 계십니다. 그리고 하나님께서 우리 안에 머물러 계시다는 것을, 우리는 그분이 우리에게 주신 성령으로 확신할 수 있습니다.
ko.R: 하나님의 계명에 순종하는 사람은 하나님 안에 머물러 있고, 하나님께서도 그 사람 안에 머물러 계십니다. 하나님께서 우리에게 주신 성령으로 우리는 하나님께서 우리 안에 머물러 계시다는 것을 압니다.

decisions.choice: his commands, in him: God, and the mutual remaining of God and the believer
decisions.reason: The commands are God's, as in 3:22-23, so "in him" is most naturally God. The two-way remaining echoes Jesus's words, "remain in me, and I in you" (John 15:4; 6:56), and returns in 4:13-16.

decisions.choice: the Spirit: the Holy Spirit
decisions.reason: πνεῦμα is God's Spirit, given to believers (4:13; John 14:16-17). This is the first mention of the Spirit in the letter, and it leads into the testing of spirits in 4:1-6.

decisions.choice: by this ... from the Spirit: the Spirit is the source of our assurance
alternatives: by this points back to keeping the commands
decisions.reason: "By this" points forward to "from the Spirit": the Spirit God has given is how we know that he remains in us. The relative pronoun is genitive because it takes the case of the word before it; it refers to the Spirit as a person.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God for the pronouns, following the meaning decision, and use the plural "those ... them" so the many pronouns stay clear.

decisions.choice: y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} en {{gender:esa persona|él}}
decisions.reason: As in John 15:5: the pronoun for God takes the deity_pronoun setting, and the one for the believer the gender setting, so the two never look alike.

decisions.choice: Roho
decisions.reason: The Spirit here is the Holy Spirit (m2), so "Roho" is written with a capital, as in John's Gospel; lowercase "roho" is kept for the human spirit and for the spirits tested in 4:1.

decisions.choice: "성령" for the Spirit
decisions.reason: The Spirit here is the Holy Spirit (meaning decision), so Korean says "성령", as the style guide sets; "영" is kept for other spirits (4:1-3).
